Requesting Provider: Dr. Sarah Kim, MD — Spine Surgery
Facility: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
Original Denial Date: November 08, 2024
Appeal Date: November 22, 2024

FINAL DISPOSITION: OVERTURNED

Dear Mr. Green,

HealthFirst has completed its review of the appeal submitted on your behalf by Dr. Sarah Kim, MD, regarding the prior authorization denial for a single-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 (CPT 22551) at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. 

After a comprehensive clinical and regulatory review of your medical records, the plan's clinical coverage criteria, and applicable California state regulations, HealthFirst has determined that the initial denial issued on November 08, 2024, by Dr. Patricia Huang, MD, is hereby OVERTURNED. Prior authorization for the requested ACDF C5-C6 procedure is APPROVED.

The decision to overturn the denial is based on two independent and sufficient grounds: (1) full clinical conformance with the plan's medical necessity criteria, and (2) critical procedural defects in the initial denial notice under California law. There is no conflict between the plan's internal criteria and the clinical/regulatory standards, as both independently and consistently support the approval of this procedure.

I. CLINICAL ANALYSIS AND CONFORMANCE WITH PLAN CRITERIA
The clinical records demonstrate that you fully satisfy all medical necessity criteria outlined in HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria for Spinal Surgery — Cervical Procedures (Document: CC-SPINE-2024, Effective January 1, 2024):

1. Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1): 
You have a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy C5-C6 with functional impairment. Your neurological examination dated September 25, 2024, documents objective neurological deficits, including left C6 dermatomal numbness, a diminished left bicep reflex, and left bicep weakness (graded 4/5). This clinical presentation is directly supported by an MRI dated September 20, 2024 (within the required 6-month window), which demonstrates a large C5-C6 disc herniation causing moderate left C6 nerve root compression. This satisfies Section 2.1(a) and Section 2.1(c).

2. Conservative Treatment Requirement (Section 2.2):
Your clinical history demonstrates the successful completion of a comprehensive course of conservative treatment that meets and exceeds all plan requirements:
- Physical Therapy (Section 2.2(a)): You completed 7 weeks of supervised physical therapy (totaling 21 sessions). The physical therapy notes document that you reached a functional plateau at week 6, with persistent radicular symptoms. This satisfies the plan's 6-week minimum requirement.
- Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)): You completed trials of two distinct classes of pharmacotherapy for more than the required 4 weeks each: (1) Gabapentin (a neuropathic agent) at 600mg TID for 4 months, which provided only partial relief, and (2) Naproxen (an NSAID) at 500mg BID for 3 months, which provided inadequate relief. This satisfies Section 2.2(b).
- Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)): You underwent a left C6 epidural steroid injection on October 28, 2024, which provided 40% temporary relief before your symptoms returned to baseline within 3 weeks. This satisfies the requirement for at least one interventional treatment under Section 2.2(c).

3. Imaging Requirement (Section 2.3):
Your MRI dated September 20, 2024, is current (within 6 months of the request) and demonstrates structural pathology (large C5-C6 disc herniation with moderate left C6 nerve root compression) that directly correlates with your clinical symptoms of left C6 radiculopathy and objective neurological deficits. This satisfies Section 2.3.

4. Physician Documentation (Section 2.4):
The clinical documentation submitted by Dr. Sarah Kim, MD, includes the necessary clinical rationale, description of functional limitations, and details of conservative treatments attempted, satisfying Section 2.4.

II. REGULATORY ANALYSIS AND PROCEDURAL DEFECTS
In addition to meeting all clinical criteria, the initial denial notice issued on November 08, 2024, contained severe procedural defects under California law that independently invalidate the denial:

1. Failure to Provide Clinical Criteria (CHSC § 1374.31):
Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(a)(2), a health plan must include the specific criteria applied and the specific clinical reasons in its written denial notice. Furthermore, CHSC § 1374.31(b) states that a denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied is defective and shall be treated as if no denial was issued. The initial denial notice referenced an attached criteria document, but no such document was attached or provided to you or Dr. Kim. This omission constitutes a major procedural violation under CHSC § 1374.31(b).

2. Omission of Independent Medical Review (IMR) Notice (CHSC § 1374.31):
CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2) mandates that all medical necessity denials include a notice of Independent Medical Review (IMR) rights. The initial denial notice failed to include the required IMR notice, violating California statutory requirements.

3. Mechanical Application of Physical Therapy Requirements (CIC § 10169.5):
Under California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(2), a health insurer shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy where the member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms. CIC § 10169.5(c) explicitly prohibits the mechanical application of a minimum number of weeks of physical therapy. Your physical therapy records clearly document a functional plateau at week 6. Any denial based on a mechanical application of physical therapy duration would violate CIC § 10169.5.

III. CLINICAL EVIDENCE STANDARDS
The clinical evidence base strongly supports surgical intervention for your presentation. According to the North American Spine Society (NASS) Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020) and the AANS/CNS Joint Section Guidelines (2023), surgical decompression via ACDF is a Tier 2 (Reasonable Indication) procedure for patients with cervical radiculopathy who exhibit objective neurological deficits (such as your documented left C6 dermatomal numbness and 4/5 bicep weakness) and persistent symptoms after an adequate trial of conservative therapy (including physical therapy, pharmacotherapy, and epidural injections). 

IV. CONCLUSION
Because you meet all clinical criteria under HealthFirst Policy CC-SPINE-2024, and because the initial denial notice was procedurally defective under CHSC § 1374.31(b), the prior authorization denial is OVERTURNED. 

An approved prior authorization has been issued for CPT 22551 (ACDF C5-C6, one level) to be performed by Dr. Sarah Kim, MD, at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. This authorization is valid for 90 days from the date of this letter, expiring on February 23, 2025, in accordance with Section 3.5 of the plan policy.

Sincerely,

Medical Director
HealthFirst Appeals and Grievance Department

**HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN — PRIOR AUTHORIZATION APPEAL DETERMINATION**

**Case ID:** PA-2024-D003
**Member:** Jessica Turner, M-556688
**Procedure:** ACDF C6-C7, one level (CPT 22551)
**Date of Denial:** 2024-10-15
**Reviewer:** Expert Health Plan Appeals Reviewer
**Date of Review:** 2024-10-26

**DISPOSITION: OVERTURN**

---

**WARRANT FOR DISPOSITION**

The denial of prior authorization for CPT code 22551 (ACDF C6-C7, one level) for member Jessica Turner is hereby **OVERTURNED**. This determination is based on a critical procedural defect in the denial notice, which violates California state law, and further, on substantive conflicts between the plan's criteria and both state law and generally accepted clinical standards of care for cervical radiculopathy.

**I. Procedural Defect in Denial Notice (State Law Violation)**

The primary and immediate basis for this overturn is the plan's failure to issue a procedurally adequate denial notice as mandated by California Health and Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(a)(2) and (b).

*   **Lack of Written Criteria and Specific Reason:** The denial explicitly states that the "written_denial_basis" was "Verbal only — peer-to-peer call," and that "Detailed criteria review provided verbally during peer-to-peer call." CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2) requires that a plan SHALL "Include in the denial notice: the specific criteria applied, the specific clinical reason for the denial, and notice of IMR rights." Communicating these details verbally during a peer-to-peer discussion does not satisfy the requirement for a *written* denial notice.
*   **Absence of IMR Notice:** The clinical record explicitly states "imr_notice_included: false." This directly violates CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2), which mandates the inclusion of IMR rights in the denial notice.
*   **Legal Consequence:** CHSC § 1374.31(b) unequivocally states: "A denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason for the denial is DEFECTIVE and shall be treated as if no denial was issued for purposes of appeal timelines." This defect renders the denial invalid from its inception, necessitating an **OVERTURN** to allow for a compliant review process.

**II. Substantive Conflicts with State Law and Clinical Standards**

Even if the procedural defects were remedied, a substantive review reveals likely conflicts with state law and generally accepted clinical standards, which would also challenge the validity of the denial.

*   **Diagnosis:** The member's presenting diagnosis is cervical radiculopathy C6-C7, confirmed by imaging (C6-C7 disc herniation, right C7 nerve root compression, moderate foraminal stenosis) and neurological exam (right C7 dermatomal numbness and tingling, diminished tricep reflex, grip 4+/5). This meets the HealthFirst Plan Criteria Section 2.1(a) for Cervical Radiculopathy. There is no evidence of cervical myelopathy (e.g., cord compression, myelomalacia, upper motor neuron signs), therefore the plan's myelopathy exception (Section 2.2(A)) is not applicable, nor are myelopathy-specific state guidance like DMHC APL 22-014 regarding myelomalacia.

*   **Physical Therapy Requirement (Conflict with State Law):**
    *   **Plan Criteria:** HealthFirst Plan Criteria Section 2.2(a) requires a "minimum 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy." The member completed 5 weeks (15 sessions).
    *   **State Law Override:** California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(2) states that a health insurer shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy where "The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms."
    *   **Application:** The member completed a course of physical therapy (5 weeks), and the treating physician explicitly "declares plateau in appeal letter." Per CIC § 10169.5(b), a "functional plateau" is determined by the treating physical therapist *or physician*. The physician's declaration in the appeal letter constitutes sufficient documentation under state law. Therefore, the plan cannot deny based solely on the duration of physical therapy, as state law overrides the plan's 6-week minimum in this circumstance.

*   **Pharmacotherapy and Interventional Treatment Requirements (Conflict with Clinical Standard):**
    *   **Plan Criteria:** HealthFirst Plan Criteria Section 2.2(b) requires "at least two... for minimum 4 weeks each" pharmacotherapy agents, and Section 2.2(c) requires "One of the following interventional treatments." The member used Meloxicam (3 months, meets 4-week duration) but Prednisone (2 weeks, does not meet 4-week duration), so only one pharmacotherapy agent met criteria. No interventional treatments were performed.
    *   **Clinical Standard:** The AANS/CNS 2023 Guidelines for Cervical Myelopathy (which also addresses radiculopathy) Section 3.1, Tier 2, states that surgery is a "Reasonable Indication" for "Radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks conservative tx." This guideline provides a broad timeframe for conservative treatment but does not mandate specific numbers or types of pharmacotherapy agents or interventional procedures.
    *   **Conflict:** With 5 weeks of PT (with a physician-declared plateau) and 3 months of NSAID therapy, the member has undergone a substantial course of conservative treatment. The plan's specific, quantitative requirements for two pharmacotherapy agents meeting a 4-week minimum *each* and a mandatory interventional procedure may be considered more restrictive than the "generally accepted standards of medical practice" for an adequate conservative trial for radiculopathy, as outlined by AANS/CNS. Under CHSC § 1374.32(b), services meeting generally accepted standards of medical practice shall be approved, regardless of whether the plan's internal criteria are more restrictive.

**III. Conclusion**

The denial by HealthFirst PPO Gold for CPT 22551 is procedurally defective under California law and is also subject to substantive challenges based on state law overrides and conflicts with generally accepted clinical standards.

**Therefore, the denial is OVERTURNED.** The plan must rescind the current denial and process the prior authorization request in a manner consistent with California law and generally accepted standards of medical practice. If the plan intends to issue a denial, it must do so with a fully compliant written notice, including specific clinical reasons, criteria, and IMR rights.

---
**Citations:**

1.  California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(a)(2)
2.  California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b)
3.  California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(2)
4.  California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(b)
5.  California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32(b)
6.  HealthFirst Plan Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Sections 2.1(a), 2.2(a), 2.2(b), 2.2(c)
7.  AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine: Guidelines for Management of Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (2023 Update), Section 3.1, Tier 2(b)
8.  Clinical Record: "presenting_diagnosis", "imaging", "neurological_exam", "conservative_treatment", "denial" details, "appeal basis", "procedural_defects" fields.
ground_truth_answer: REMAND — The clinical denial may be substantively correct (5 weeks PT vs 6 required, no injection, plateau not formally documented in PT records). However, CHSC 1374.31(b) requires written criteria in the denial notice. Verbal peer-to-peer communication cannot substitute for written notice. Plan must reissue a compliant written denial.
genuine_tension: Clinical criteria not met on the merits — 5 weeks PT, no injection, plateau not formally documented. The denial is substantively defensible. But the procedural violation (criteria communicated verbally only, no IMR notice) independently requires remedy.

*   **Plan Year / Coverage Effective:** 2024 / 2023-07-01
*   **Requested Procedure:** Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7, One Level (CPT 22551)
*   **Requesting Physician:** Dr. Robert Chen, MD — Spine Surgery
*   **Facility:** Stanford Medical Center
*   **Prior Authorization Denial Date:** October 15, 2024
*   **Reviewing Medical Director (Initial):** Dr. Alan Foster, MD

---

### FINAL DETERMINATION DISPOSITION

**DISPOSITION: OVERTURNED**

The initial decision to deny coverage for CPT 22551 (ACDF C6-C7) at Stanford Medical Center is **OVERTURNED**. Prior authorization is hereby **APPROVED** for the requested surgical procedure on **procedural and regulatory grounds**, which supersede the plan’s internal clinical criteria under California law.

---

### 1. PROCEDURAL ADEQUACY AND REGULATORY COMPLIANCE CHECK (CHSC § 1374.31)

Under the **Hierarchy of Authority** established for this review, California State Law represents the supreme governing authority, superseding both national clinical guidelines and internal plan criteria:
$$\text{California State Law (CIC, CHSC, DMHC APL)} > \text{Generally Accepted Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS, AO Spine)} > \text{Plan Criteria (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024)}$$

A rigorous procedural review of the initial denial issued on October 15, 2024, reveals critical statutory violations under **California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31**:

*   **Statutory Requirement (CHSC § 1374.31(a)):** When a health plan issues a denial based on medical necessity, it must provide a written notice of the denial that specifies the clinical criteria applied, the specific clinical reasons for the denial, and includes the mandatory notice of Independent Medical Review (IMR) rights.
*   **Procedural Deficiencies in Initial Denial:**
    1.  **Failure to Provide Written Criteria/Clinical Reasons:** The plan’s written denial notice dated October 15, 2024, did not specify the clinical criteria or clinical reasons in writing. Instead, it stated: *"Request denied based on peer-to-peer review... Detailed criteria review provided verbally during peer-to-peer call."* Verbal communication during a peer-to-peer call does not satisfy the statutory mandate for written disclosure.
    2.  **Omission of Mandatory IMR Notice:** The plan failed to include the legally required IMR notice, which is a direct violation of CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2).
*   **Statutory Penalty (CHSC § 1374.31(b)):** The statute explicitly states that a denial notice failing to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason for the denial is **defective** and **"shall be treated as if no denial was issued."**

**Finding:** The initial denial is **procedurally defective and legally invalid**. Because the plan failed to issue a legally compliant written denial, the denial is voided. On procedural grounds alone, the denial must be **OVERTURNED** (Condition A).

---

### 2. DIAGNOSIS AND PATHOLOGY CLASSIFICATION

The clinical record has been evaluated to differentiate between cervical radiculopathy and cervical myelopathy, as these conditions represent distinct clinical pathways:

*   **Imaging Findings (MRI dated 2024-09-01):** Demonstrates a C6-C7 disc herniation, right C7 nerve root compression, and moderate foraminal stenosis. There is no evidence of spinal cord compression or T2 cord signal changes (myelomalacia).
*   **Neurological Exam Findings (dated 2024-09-05):** Reveals right C7 dermatomal numbness and tingling, a diminished right triceps reflex, and right hand grip strength of 4+/5. There are no upper motor neuron signs (e.g., no Hoffman sign, no hyperreflexia, no gait disturbance, and no bilateral symptoms).
*   **Classification:**
    *   **Radiculopathy (Confirmed):** The patient's pathology is strictly unilateral, dermatomal, and consistent with lower motor neuron nerve root compression at C6-C7.
    *   **Myelopathy (Absent):** There is zero clinical or radiographic evidence of cervical myelopathy or spinal cord injury (myelomalacia).

**Finding:** The member has a confirmed diagnosis of **cervical radiculopathy (C6-C7)**. This is a **Negative Finding for Myelopathy** under Plan Section 2.1. The clinical presentation is that of an elective radiculopathy rather than a progressive myelopathic emergency.

---

### 3. STATUTORY AND REGULATORY CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT WAIVERS (CIC § 10169.5 & DMHC APL 22-014)

Because the member has cervical radiculopathy without cord compression or myelomalacia, the automatic clinical urgency waivers under **DMHC All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014** and **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(3)** (structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address) are **not triggered**. 

However, **CIC § 10169.5** contains other provisions regarding physical therapy as a prerequisite:

*   **CIC § 10169.5(a)(2):** A health insurer shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy if the member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a **functional plateau** without adequate resolution of symptoms.
*   **CIC § 10169.5(c):** A plan’s internal requirement for a minimum number of weeks of physical therapy **shall not be applied mechanically** without reference to whether the member has achieved a functional plateau.
*   **Application to Case:** The member completed 5 weeks (15 sessions) of supervised physical therapy. Although a functional plateau was not formally documented in the physical therapist's discharge notes, the treating spine surgeon (Dr. Chen) explicitly documented and declared a clinical functional plateau in the appeal submission. Under California law, this physician documentation is sufficient to satisfy the plateau exception, overriding the plan's rigid 6-week minimum requirement.

---

### 4. CLINICAL STANDARDS AND EVIDENCE-BASED GUIDELINES (AANS/CNS 2023 & AO SPINE 2021)

Under **CHSC § 1374.32(b)**, clinical standards of medical practice govern independent review and override more restrictive plan-specific policies:

*   **AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023):** For cervical radiculopathy, surgical decompression (ACDF) is classified as a **Tier 2 - Reasonable Indication** when the patient presents with persistent dermatomal pain, numbness, or weakness that has failed to respond to an appropriate trial of conservative therapy (typically 6 to 12 weeks of combined modalities).
*   **Clinical Timeline Analysis:** The member has been undergoing conservative management for over 12 weeks, consisting of:
    *   **3 months (12 weeks)** of Meloxicam 15mg daily (NSAID pharmacotherapy), yielding only partial relief.
    *   **2 weeks** of an oral Prednisone taper, yielding only temporary improvement.
    *   **5 weeks (15 sessions)** of structured physical therapy.
*   **Clinical Appropriateness:** While the patient does not present with a Tier 1 myelopathic emergency, she has failed to achieve lasting relief from extensive oral pharmacotherapy and a near-complete physical therapy trial, and has objective, matching neurological deficits (C7 sensory loss, reflex change, and motor weakness). Surgical decompression is clinically appropriate and aligned with generally accepted standards of care.

---

### 5. PLAN-SPECIFIC CRITERIA AND EXCEPTION APPLICATION (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024)

An evaluation of the request against the plan's internal medical policy (**CC-SPINE-2024**) indicates:

1.  **Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1):** Met. Confirmed cervical radiculopathy (C6-C7) supported by an MRI within 6 months.
2.  **Myelopathy Exception (Section 2.2(A)):** **Not Applicable.** The primary diagnosis is radiculopathy; myelopathy is not present. Therefore, standard conservative treatment criteria apply.
3.  **Standard Conservative Treatment Requirements (Section 2.2):**
    *   *Physical Therapy:* **Unmet.** Completed 5 weeks (15 sessions); policy requires a minimum of 6 weeks.
    *   *Pharmacotherapy:* **Unmet.** Completed a 3-month trial of Meloxicam (NSAID), but the second agent (Prednisone) was only trialed for 2 weeks. Policy requires a trial of two agents for a *minimum of 4 weeks each*.
    *   *Interventional Treatment:* **Unmet.** No epidural steroid injections or blocks were performed. Policy requires at least one interventional procedure.

**Finding:** The clinical request **fails to satisfy the standard internal criteria** of HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2.

---

### 6. HIERARCHICAL SYNTHESIS AND RESOLUTION

To resolve the conflict between the unmet plan-specific criteria and the procedural/regulatory requirements, we apply the mandatory **Hierarchy of Authority**:

1.  **Plan Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024):** Strict adherence would dictate an Uphold, as the member did not complete 6 weeks of PT, 4 weeks of a second oral medication, or an interventional trial.
2.  **Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS):** Suggests that 12 weeks of persistent radicular pain with motor deficit and matching MRI findings represents a reasonable surgical indication, and extending conservative management risks prolonging neurological deficit (grip weakness).
3.  **California State Law (CHSC & CIC):** Serves as the supreme authority. Under **CHSC § 1374.31(b)**, the plan's initial denial is legally defective due to the failure to cite written criteria, the failure to provide written clinical reasons, and the omission of IMR rights. The statute mandates that this defect be treated **as if no denial was issued**. Additionally, **CIC § 10169.5** prohibits the mechanical application of a 6-week PT rule when a physician documents a functional plateau (which occurred at week 5).

Because California statutory law invalidates the plan's initial denial and prohibits the mechanical enforcement of the 6-week physical therapy requirement, the plan's internal criteria are legally superseded. 

### CONCLUSION

The prior authorization denial was issued in a procedurally defective manner under California law. Furthermore, the clinical record establishes that the member has a matching radiographic and clinical radiculopathy with objective neurological deficits that have reached a functional plateau after 5 weeks of physical therapy and 3 months of pharmacotherapy. 

Pursuant to **CHSC § 1374.31** and **CIC § 10169.5**, the initial denial is **OVERTURNED**, and the request for CPT 22551 (ACDF C6-C7) is **APPROVED**.

**Authorized Service:** CPT Code 22551 (Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion, C6-C7)
**Facility:** Stanford Medical Center
**Requesting Provider:** Dr. Robert Chen, MD
**Coverage Effective Date:** October 15, 2024 (valid for 90 days per policy terms)
ground_truth_answer: REMAND — The clinical denial may be substantively correct (5 weeks PT vs 6 required, no injection, plateau not formally documented in PT records). However, CHSC 1374.31(b) requires written criteria in the denial notice. Verbal peer-to-peer communication cannot substitute for written notice. Plan must reissue a compliant written denial.
genuine_tension: Clinical criteria not met on the merits — 5 weeks PT, no injection, plateau not formally documented. The denial is substantively defensible. But the procedural violation (criteria communicated verbally only, no IMR notice) independently requires remedy.

**HealthFirst Health Plan — Appeal Determination Letter**

**Case ID:** PA-2024-E001
**Member:** Victor Patel, M-667799
**Procedure:** ACDF C5-C6 and C6-C7, two levels (CPT 22552)
**Requested by:** Dr. Lisa Park, MD
**Facility:** UCSF Medical Center
**Date of Initial Denial:** 2024-11-01
**Reason for Denial:** "Two-level fusion not supported. C5-C6 level shows pathology consistent with surgical criteria. C6-C7 shows mild changes only. Two-level fusion not approved when one level meets criteria and one does not."
**Appeal Basis:** ["Both levels are symptomatic per treating physician", "Adjacent levels should be addressed simultaneously to prevent accelerated degeneration", "Member meets full criteria for both levels"]
**Reviewer:** [Your Name/Title - Expert Appeals Reviewer]
**Date of Appeal Determination:** 2024-11-15

---

**I. Overview of Appeal and Clinical Record**

This appeal concerns a prior authorization request for a two-level anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 and C6-C7 for member Victor Patel. The initial denial cited a lack of medical necessity for the C6-C7 level. The appealing party argues that both levels are symptomatic, adjacent levels should be treated simultaneously, and both levels meet full criteria.

The clinical record indicates:
*   **Presenting Diagnosis:** Two-level cervical disc disease C5-C6 and C6-C7 with asymmetric severity.
*   **Imaging (MRI 2024-09-15):**
    *   C5-C6: Large disc herniation, moderate-severe right C6 nerve root compression, foraminal stenosis.
    *   C6-C7: Small disc bulge, mild foraminal narrowing, no nerve root compression identifiable, no cord contact.
*   **Neurological Exam (2024-09-20):**
    *   C6 level: Right bicep weakness 3+/5, bicep reflex absent right, right C6 dermatomal numbness and tingling.
    *   C7 level: Right tricep reflex slightly diminished. No definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms. Physician notes mild C7 symptoms *possibly* present but not clearly documented.
*   **Conservative Treatment:**
    *   Physical Therapy: 8 weeks, 24 sessions. C6 symptoms persist. C7 symptoms: minimal and *possibly resolving* per PT note at week 8.
    *   Pharmacotherapy: Pregabalin (4 months, partial C6 relief), Naproxen (3 months, moderate relief).
    *   Interventional: Right C6 epidural (good C6 relief, returned in 4 weeks). **No C7-specific injection performed.**

---

**II. Application of Three-Source Hierarchy: State Law > Clinical Standard > Plan Criteria**

**A. Procedural Adequacy of Initial Denial:**
The initial denial notice clearly stated the reason for denial (C6-C7 not supported) and the specific problem (mild changes at C6-C7, lack of pathology to support two-level fusion). This meets the requirements of CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2) for specifying the clinical reason for denial.

**B. Assessment for C5-C6 Level:**
1.  **HealthFirst Plan Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024):**
    *   **2.1 Diagnosis Requirement:** Met. MRI shows large disc herniation with moderate-severe right C6 nerve root compression, and neurological exam shows objective C6 radiculopathy (weakness 3+/5, absent reflex, dermatomal numbness). This meets 2.1(a) and 2.1(c).
    *   **2.2 Conservative Treatment Requirement:** Met. Member completed 8 weeks of physical therapy (2.2a, exceeding 6-week minimum), trials of Pregabalin and Naproxen for over 4 weeks each (2.2b), and one C6 epidural steroid injection (2.2c).
    *   **2.3 Imaging Requirement:** Met. MRI demonstrates structural pathology consistent with symptoms.
2.  **California State Law:**
    *   **CIC § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy Prerequisite):** The member completed 8 weeks of PT, and C6 symptoms persist. This indicates a functional plateau per CIC § 10169.5(a)(2), meaning even if the plan's 6-week minimum was challenged, the requirement for PT has been satisfied in this case.
    *   **DMHC APL 22-014 (Myelopathy Exception):** Not applicable, as the member's presentation for C5-C6 is radiculopathy, not myelopathy. No myelomalacia is noted.
3.  **Clinical Standard (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020):**
    *   Surgery for C5-C6 is indicated. The persistent C6 radiculopathy with objective weakness (3+/5) and absent reflex after 8 weeks of conservative treatment, including an epidural, meets Tier 1(b) (Progressive neurological deficit despite conservative treatment) or Tier 2(b) (Radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks conservative treatment) surgical indications.

    **Conclusion for C5-C6:** Surgical intervention at C5-C6 is medically necessary and meets all plan criteria, state law, and generally accepted clinical standards. The initial denial reviewer acknowledged this, stating "C5-C6 level shows pathology consistent with surgical criteria."

**C. Assessment for C6-C7 Level:**
1.  **HealthFirst Plan Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024):**
    *   **2.1 Diagnosis Requirement:** Not met. The MRI at C6-C7 shows "small disc bulge, mild foraminal narrowing, no nerve root compression identifiable, no cord contact." The neurological exam shows "no definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms" and only a "slightly diminished tricep reflex." This does not meet the criteria for cervical radiculopathy (2.1a) or cervical myelopathy (2.1b), nor does it constitute a "disc herniation with objective neurological deficit" (2.1c) at this specific level.
    *   **2.2 Conservative Treatment Requirement:** Not met. While PT and pharmacotherapy were administered, a C7-specific interventional treatment (2.2c) was *not* performed. This would be required if C6-C7 otherwise qualified for surgery.
    *   **2.3 Imaging Requirement:** Not met. The imaging findings ("mild changes only," "no nerve root compression identifiable," "no cord contact") are not consistent with a need for surgical intervention based on the clinical presentation for C6-C7, which lacks definitive symptoms.
    *   **Myelopathy Exception (2.2A):** Not applicable. The clinical record does not indicate myelopathy at C6-C7; there is no spinal cord compression or myelopathic symptoms.
2.  **California State Law:**
    *   **CIC § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy Prerequisite):** While 8 weeks of PT was completed, the PT note states C7 symptoms were "minimal and possibly resolving." This does not suggest a functional plateau of *significant* symptoms requiring surgery. The lack of definitive C7 pathology means the exemption for "structural neurological compromise" (a)(3) also does not apply.
    *   **DMHC APL 22-014 (Myelopathy and Urgent Conditions):** Not applicable. There is no evidence of myelopathy, myelomalacia, or urgent progressive pathology at C6-C7.
    *   **CHSC § 1374.32(b) (IMR Standard):** This provision would allow approval if clinical standards are met, even if plan criteria are more restrictive. However, as detailed below, clinical standards are *not* met for C6-C7.
3.  **Clinical Standard (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021):**
    *   **Section 3.1 Accepted Indications for ACDF:** C6-C7 does not meet any Tier 1 or Tier 2 surgical indications. There is no moderate-severe myelopathy, progressive neurological deficit, myelomalacia, or radiculopathy with persistent symptoms. A "small disc bulge" and "mild foraminal narrowing" without objective nerve root compression or definitive clinical symptoms are not considered surgical indications under generally accepted standards of medical practice.
    *   **Adjacent Level Degeneration (Appeal Basis):** While addressing adjacent levels may be considered in some cases of definite, albeit mild, symptomatic pathology, operating on an asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic level lacking objective nerve root compression to prevent future degeneration is not a generally accepted surgical indication.

    **Conclusion for C6-C7:** Surgical intervention at C6-C7 is not medically necessary based on HealthFirst's plan criteria, state law, or generally accepted clinical standards. The appeal basis that "Both levels are symptomatic" and "Member meets full criteria for both levels" is not supported by the clinical record for C6-C7.

**D. Conflict Resolution:**
There is no conflict between the plan's criteria, state law, or clinical standards regarding the C6-C7 level. All sources consistently indicate that a fusion at C6-C7 is not medically necessary given the current clinical presentation and imaging findings.

---

**III. Disposition**

The request was for a two-level ACDF (CPT 22552) at C5-C6 and C6-C7. Based on the comprehensive review, only the C5-C6 level meets the criteria for surgical intervention. The C6-C7 level does not meet medical necessity criteria under plan guidelines, state law, or generally accepted clinical standards. Therefore, the denial of the *two-level* fusion as requested is appropriate.

**Disposition: UPHOLD DENIAL of two-level ACDF (CPT 22552).**

**Warrant:**
The denial for a two-level ACDF is UPHELD because the C6-C7 level does not demonstrate medical necessity for surgical fusion, consistent with HealthFirst Plan Clinical Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024, Sections 2.1, 2.2c, 2.3) and generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS 2023 Guidelines, Section 3.1). The MRI findings for C6-C7 show only "small disc bulge, mild foraminal narrowing, no nerve root compression identifiable, no cord contact," which does not constitute a surgical indication. Furthermore, the neurological exam at the C7 level revealed "no definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms" and only a "slightly diminished tricep reflex," which is insufficient to warrant surgery per clinical guidelines. Additionally, a C7-specific interventional treatment was not performed, failing a requirement of the plan's conservative treatment criteria (CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2c). State laws such as DMHC APL 22-014 and CIC § 10169.5 do not override these findings as they primarily address myelopathy or PT completion for *medically indicated* conditions, neither of which applies to C6-C7 in this case.

While the C5-C6 level clearly meets criteria for surgical intervention (consistent with CC-SPINE-2024, Sections 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 and AANS/CNS 2023 Guidelines, Section 3.1, Tiers 1b/2b), the request was for a specific two-level procedure (CPT 22552). Since one of the requested levels does not meet medical necessity, the denial of the *two-level* procedure as submitted is upheld. The treating physician may submit a new prior authorization request for a single-level ACDF at C5-C6 (CPT 22551).

---
**Right to Independent Medical Review (IMR):**
You have the right to request an Independent Medical Review (IMR) of this decision. An IMR is a review by an independent medical expert to determine if the requested service is medically necessary under generally accepted standards of medical practice, regardless of the plan's internal criteria (CHSC § 1374.32(b)). You may apply for IMR by contacting the California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) within 180 days of this determination. Information on how to apply for an IMR can be found on the DMHC website or by calling their toll-free number.
ground_truth_answer: PARTIAL — OVERTURN for C5-C6 (large herniation, moderate-severe compression, clear C6 neurological deficit, failed conservative treatment). REMAND for C6-C7 (mild imaging findings, equivocal exam findings, possibly resolving symptoms per PT notes — insufficient documentation to approve at this time). A bilateral epidural injection targeting both levels should be tried before C6-C7 is reconsidered.
genuine_tension: C5-C6 is unambiguously indicated. C6-C7 is genuinely borderline — mild imaging changes, equivocal exam, possibly resolving symptoms. Binary OVERTURN approves both levels when one is questionable. Binary UPHOLD denies both when one is clearly indicated. The correct answer is PARTIAL.

determination:
# FORMAL APPEAL DETERMINATION

**CASE ID:** PA-2024-E001  
**MEMBER:** Victor Patel (ID: M-667799)  
**AGE:** 60  
**PLAN:** HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441  
**STATE OF JURISDICTION:** California  
**PLAN YEAR:** 2024  
**COVERAGE EFFECTIVE DATE:** May 1, 2016  
**REQUESTED PROCEDURE:** Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF), C5–C6 and C6–C7, Two Levels (CPT 22551 and CPT 22552)  
**REQUESTING PHYSICIAN:** Dr. Lisa Park, MD — Spine Surgery, UCSF Medical Center  
**INITIAL DENIAL DATE:** November 1, 2024  
**INITIAL REVIEWER:** Dr. Patricia Huang, MD  
**DETERMINATION DATE:** November 18, 2024  

---

## I. FINAL DISPOSITION
Pursuant to California Health and Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32 and generally accepted standards of medical practice, the initial denial is **PARTIALLY OVERTURNED and PARTIALLY UPHELD**. 

*   **CPT Code 22551** (Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion, C5–C6, Single Level) is **APPROVED**. The initial denial of this level is **OVERTURNED**.
*   **CPT Code 22552** (ACDF, C6–C7, adjacent/additional level) is **DENIED**. The initial denial of this level is **UPHELD**.

---

## II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Dr. Lisa Park requested a two-level ACDF (C5–C6 and C6–C7). The plan initially issued a blanket denial of the entire request because one level (C6–C7) did not meet clinical criteria. 

This review finds that the initial denial notice was **procedurally defective** under California law for failing to cite the specific clinical coverage criteria applied. Substantively, the medical record demonstrates that the member has severe, symptomatic **right C6 cervical radiculopathy** with objective neurological deficits (3+/5 bicep weakness, absent bicep reflex) and correlating MRI pathology at C5–C6. The member has fully completed the plan’s standard conservative treatment trials (8 weeks of PT, 2 pharmacotherapy agents, and an epidural steroid injection with temporary relief). Fusing C5–C6 is clinically indicated and medically necessary. 

Conversely, the adjacent C6–C7 level exhibits only mild, age-related changes on MRI without nerve root or spinal cord compression, and lacks correlating neurological deficits or symptoms. Multi-level fusion is not indicated solely to prevent "adjacent segment degeneration" in the absence of active, correlating pathology. Therefore, surgical intervention at C6–C7 is denied.

---

## III. NUMBERED EVALUATION & CLINICAL ANALYSIS

### 1. Procedural Defect Check (CHSC § 1374.31(b))
*   **Analysis**: Under California Health & Safety Code § 1374.31(b), a plan’s written denial must explicitly cite the specific clinical coverage criteria applied, specify the clinical reasons for the denial, and provide notice of Independent Medical Review (IMR) rights. The initial denial notice issued on November 1, 2024, failed to cite the applicable plan document (**HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024**) and failed to provide a notice of IMR rights, stating only that a "two-level fusion is not supported" due to mild changes at C6–C7. 
*   **Finding**: **POSITIVE FINDING OF PROCEDURAL DEFECT**. The denial notice is procedurally defective. Under CHSC § 1374.31(b), a defective notice "shall be treated as if no denial was issued" regarding appeal timelines. However, to protect member safety and ensure clinical appropriateness under CHSC § 1374.32(b), this review proceeds to evaluate the clinical merits of each level to avoid authorizing an unnecessary and potentially harmful secondary fusion.

### 2. Clinical Classification and Diagnostic Verification
*   **Analysis**: The clinical record was evaluated to classify the pathology as either cervical radiculopathy or cervical myelopathy:
    *   *Myelopathy Indicators*: The MRI of September 15, 2024, shows no spinal cord compression, no cord contact, and no myelomalacia (T2 cord signal changes). The neurological exam of September 20, 2024, lists no bilateral symptoms, no upper motor neuron (UMN) signs (e.g., positive Hoffman, hyperreflexia, clonus, or gait disturbance), and no bowel/bladder dysfunction.
    *   *Radiculopathy Indicators*: The member presents with unilateral (right) bicep weakness (3+/5), an absent right bicep reflex, and right C6 dermatomal numbness and tingling. The C5–C6 MRI shows a large disc herniation, moderate-to-severe right C6 nerve root compression, and foraminal stenosis.
*   **Finding**: **NEGATIVE FINDING FOR MYELOPATHY**. The primary diagnosis is verified as **severe unilateral right C6 cervical radiculopathy** originating from the C5–C6 level. The case is evaluated under standard conservative treatment pathways (Step 4, negative pathway).

### 3. Imaging Correlation and Multi-Level Pathology Analysis
*   **Analysis**: 
    *   **C5–C6 Level**: MRI findings of a large disc herniation and moderate-severe right C6 nerve root compression directly correlate with the member's clinical presentation of right bicep weakness (3+/5), absent bicep reflex, and C6 numbness.
    *   **C6–C7 Level**: MRI shows only a small disc bulge and mild foraminal narrowing, with no identifiable nerve root compression and no cord contact. The neurological exam reveals a slightly diminished tricep reflex but no definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms. Dr. Park noted that C7 symptoms were "possibly present but not clearly documented," and the physical therapy discharge note from week 8 reports that C7-related symptoms were "minimal and possibly resolving."
*   **Finding**: **NEGATIVE FINDING FOR MULTI-LEVEL PATHOLOGY**. While C5–C6 shows severe, clinically correlating pathology, the C6–C7 level shows only mild, age-related changes without structural nerve root compression or correlating clinical symptoms. Under Plan Criteria Section 3.3 and AANS/CNS clinical guidelines, surgery at the C6–C7 level (CPT 22552) is not clinically indicated.

### 4. Statutory Overrides of Conservative Treatment Requirements
*   **Analysis**: 
    *   Because there is no objective spinal cord compression or myelomalacia, the automatic statutory exceptions to conservative treatment under **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(3)** and **DMHC APL 22-014** do not apply to waive conservative trials.
    *   Therefore, standard Plan Criteria Section 2.2 applies. We must verify if the member completed the standard conservative trial:
        1.  *Physical Therapy*: Completed 8 weeks (24 sessions) of supervised PT with persisting C6 symptoms. (Plan requirement: 6 weeks; **MET**).
        2.  *Pharmacotherapy*: Taken Pregabalin 150mg BID for 4 months and Naproxen 500mg BID for 3 months. (Plan requirement: 2 agents for 4+ weeks each; **MET**).
        3.  *Interventional*: Received a right C6 epidural steroid injection on October 15, 2024, yielding 70% relief that fully returned after 4 weeks. (Plan requirement: 1 interventional procedure; **MET**).
*   **Finding**: **POSITIVE FINDING FOR PRIMARY LEVEL (C5–C6)**. The member has fully satisfied the conservative treatment requirements under Plan Criteria Section 2.2. The plan’s initial reviewer erred by denying the entire procedure based on C6–C7 pathology deficiencies, ignoring that the primary level (C5–C6) fully met all medical necessity and conservative treatment criteria.

### 5. Clinical Standards Evaluation (CHSC § 1374.32(b))
*   **Analysis**: Under California law, clinical standards of care override restrictive or improperly applied plan criteria. 
    *   **C5–C6 (CPT 22551)**: Under **AANS/CNS 2023 Guidelines (Tier 2)** and **NASS 2020 Guidelines**, single-level anterior cervical decompression and fusion (ACDF) is strongly indicated for cervical radiculopathy with objective neurological deficits (3+/5 bicep weakness, absent bicep reflex) that has failed a comprehensive 6-to-12 week conservative trial. Continuing conservative care in the presence of a motor deficit (3+/5 weakness) poses a risk of permanent neurological loss. Surgical decompression is medically necessary.
    *   **C6–C7 (CPT 22552)**: Dr. Park’s appeal basis argues that adjacent levels should be fused simultaneously to prevent accelerated degeneration. However, **AANS/CNS 2023** and **AO Spine 2021** clinical standards do not support prophylactic fusion of adjacent segments. Fusing a level with only mild, stable, or resolving symptoms and no structural nerve root compression (Tier 3) is inappropriate. It unnecessarily increases surgical morbidity, extends recovery times, and accelerates adjacent segment disease at C4–C5 and C7–T1.
*   **Finding**: **PARTIAL CLINICAL INDICATION**. Clinical standards support immediate surgical intervention for C5–C6 (CPT 22551) but contraindicate surgery at C6–C7 (CPT 22552).

---

## IV. CONCLUSION AND ORDER

Applying the **California Hierarchy of Authority** ($\text{State Law} > \text{Clinical Standards} > \text{Plan Criteria}$):

1.  **CPT 22551 (ACDF C5–C6)**: The member met all criteria in **HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2**. Furthermore, under **AANS/CNS 2023 Clinical Standards**, surgical decompression is the required standard of care for a persistent motor deficit (3+/5 bicep weakness) post-conservative therapy. The plan's decision to deny the medically necessary C5–C6 level because the secondary level was unindicated is substantively incorrect and is **OVERTURNED**.
2.  **CPT 22552 (ACDF C6–C7)**: This level does not meet medical necessity under **HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 Section 3.3** or **AANS/CNS 2023 Clinical Standards** due to a lack of correlating structural pathology, nerve compression, or clinical deficits. Prophylactic fusion is clinically unsupported. The plan's denial of this level is **UPHELD**.

**Ordered**: HealthFirst shall immediately authorize **CPT code 22551** for ACDF at the C5–C6 level, to be performed by Dr. Lisa Park at UCSF Medical Center. The request for the additional level, **CPT code 22552** (C6–C7), remains denied.

---
**Reviewer:**  
*California Board-Certified Peer Reviewer*  
*Expert Medical Reviewer, Spinal Surgery Appeals Division*
ground_truth_answer: PARTIAL — OVERTURN for C5-C6 (large herniation, moderate-severe compression, clear C6 neurological deficit, failed conservative treatment). REMAND for C6-C7 (mild imaging findings, equivocal exam findings, possibly resolving symptoms per PT notes — insufficient documentation to approve at this time). A bilateral epidural injection targeting both levels should be tried before C6-C7 is reconsidered.
genuine_tension: C5-C6 is unambiguously indicated. C6-C7 is genuinely borderline — mild imaging changes, equivocal exam, possibly resolving symptoms. Binary OVERTURN approves both levels when one is questionable. Binary UPHOLD denies both when one is clearly indicated. The correct answer is PARTIAL.

FINAL DISPOSITION: REMAND

APPEAL DETERMINATION SERVICES
CALIFORNIA DIVISION OF MEDICINE AND REGULATORY COMPLIANCE

Date: November 1, 2024

CASE IDENTIFICATION:
Case ID: PA-2024-D003
Appeal Date: October 30, 2024
Member Name: Jessica Turner
Age: 39
Member ID: M-556688
Plan: HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
State of Residence: California
Requested Procedure: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7, Single Level (CPT 22551)
Requesting Physician: Dr. Robert Chen, MD — Spine Surgery
Facility: Stanford Medical Center
Prior Authorization Denial Date: October 15, 2024
Denial Reviewer: Dr. Alan Foster, MD (Initial Review)

DISPOSITION:
The prior authorization denial for Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7 (CPT 22551) is hereby REMANDED to HealthFirst Health Plan. The plan is ordered to immediately vacate its initial denial and re-evaluate the request in accordance with California statutory requirements and the instructions detailed in this determination.

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
On October 15, 2024, HealthFirst Health Plan issued an initial denial of prior authorization for a single-level ACDF at C6-C7 (CPT 22551) requested by Dr. Robert Chen on behalf of Jessica Turner. The plan's written denial notice cited "MED-003" and stated that the request was denied based on a peer-to-peer discussion between the plan's medical director, Dr. Alan Foster, and the requesting physician, during which verbal criteria were discussed. The member appealed on October 30, 2024, on the grounds that the plan failed to provide written clinical criteria in the denial notice, in violation of California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31.

A review of the clinical record reveals that the member does not fully satisfy the plan's internal clinical coverage criteria (CC-SPINE-2024) due to shortfalls in conservative therapy (5 weeks of physical therapy completed versus 6 weeks required, lack of interventional treatment, and a 2-week prednisone trial versus the 4-week requirement). However, the plan's denial notice is critically and fatally defective under California law because the clinical criteria were communicated verbally only, and the mandatory Independent Medical Review (IMR) notice was omitted. Furthermore, the plan mechanically applied its 6-week physical therapy requirement in violation of California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5, failing to evaluate the treating physician's written declaration of a functional plateau. 

Because a defective denial notice under CHSC § 1374.31(b) must be treated as if no denial was issued, and because statutory regulatory requirements supersede conflicting plan criteria, this case is REMANDED to the plan for immediate re-evaluation and reissuance of a legally compliant determination.

II. CLINICAL PRESENTATION AND RECORD REVIEW
The clinical record submitted for review contains the following objective findings:
1. Presenting Diagnosis: Cervical radiculopathy at C6-C7.
2. Diagnostic Imaging: An MRI of the cervical spine dated September 1, 2024, demonstrates a C6-C7 disc herniation, right C7 nerve root compression, and moderate foraminal stenosis.
3. Neurological Examination: A physical and neurological exam dated September 5, 2024, reveals objective neurological deficits, including right C7 dermatomal numbness and tingling, a diminished tricep reflex, and right hand grip strength of 4+/5.
4. Conservative Treatment History:
   - Physical Therapy: The member completed 5 weeks of supervised physical therapy (total of 15 sessions). While a formal plateau was not documented in the physical therapist's daily notes, the treating physician, Dr. Robert Chen, explicitly declared in the appeal letter that the member had reached a functional plateau.
   - Pharmacotherapy: The member completed a 3-month trial of Meloxicam (15mg daily), which provided only partial relief. The member also completed a 2-week oral prednisone taper, which yielded only temporary improvement.
   - Interventional Treatment: No cervical epidural steroid injections, medial branch blocks, or trigger point injections have been performed.

III. PLAN CRITERIA COMPLIANCE ANALYSIS
Under HealthFirst Health Plan's Clinical Coverage Criteria for Spinal Surgery (Document: CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2), authorization for CPT 22551 requires that all medical necessity criteria be satisfied:
1. Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1): The member meets Section 2.1(a) (Cervical radiculopathy with nerve root compression and radicular symptoms) and Section 2.1(c) (Cervical disc herniation with objective neurological deficit), supported by the MRI dated September 1, 2024, and the neurological exam dated September 5, 2024.
2. Conservative Treatment Requirement (Section 2.2):
   - Physical Therapy (Section 2.2(a)): The plan requires a minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy. The member completed only 5 weeks, representing a 1-week shortfall.
   - Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)): The plan requires a trial of at least two specified agents for a minimum of 4 weeks each. While the member's 3-month trial of Meloxicam (NSAID) satisfies the first agent requirement, the 2-week prednisone taper (oral corticosteroid) falls short of the 4-week minimum duration required for the second agent.
   - Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)): The plan requires at least one interventional treatment (e.g., cervical epidural steroid injection). The member has had none.
3. Myelopathy Pathway Exception (Section 2.2 Exception): This exception is inapplicable because the member's primary diagnosis is cervical radiculopathy, and there is no documented diagnosis of cervical myelopathy or myelomalacia.

Consequently, under a strict, mechanical reading of the plan's internal criteria, the clinical record does not satisfy the conservative treatment requirements of Section 2.2, and the request would be subject to denial under Section 3.2.

IV. REGULATORY COMPLIANCE AND STATUTORY VIOLATIONS
Under California law, statutory and regulatory mandates govern prior authorization processes and supersede any conflicting internal plan guidelines. The plan's initial review and denial of this request involved multiple critical statutory violations:

1. Defective Denial Notice under CHSC § 1374.31(a) and (b)
California Health & Safety Code § 1374.31(a) mandates that when a plan issues a denial based on medical necessity, it "SHALL... [p]rovide written notice of the denial" which must "[i]nclude in the denial notice: the specific criteria applied, the specific clinical reason for the denial, and notice of IMR rights."
In this case, the plan's written denial notice dated October 15, 2024, failed to include any of these elements. Instead, the plan relied on a verbal peer-to-peer call between Dr. Alan Foster and Dr. Robert Chen to communicate the clinical criteria.
CHSC § 1374.31(b) explicitly states: "A denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason for the denial is DEFECTIVE and shall be treated as if no denial was issued for purposes of appeal timelines." Verbal communication during a peer-to-peer call cannot substitute for a written denial notice. Because the plan failed to document the specific clinical criteria and reasons in writing, the denial notice is legally defective and invalid.

2. Omission of Mandatory Independent Medical Review (IMR) Notice
CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2) requires the plan to include a notice of the member's right to an Independent Medical Review (IMR) in every medical necessity denial. The plan's denial notice completely omitted this notice, representing a major procedural violation that deprives the member of their statutory rights.

3. Violation of Physical Therapy Conditioning under CIC § 10169.5
California Insurance Code § 10169.5(a) provides that a health insurer "shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy where... (2) [t]he member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms."
Furthermore, CIC § 10169.5(c) prohibits plans from mechanically applying a minimum number of weeks of physical therapy without reference to whether a functional plateau has been reached.
Here, the member completed 5 weeks (15 sessions) of physical therapy, and the treating physician, Dr. Robert Chen, documented in writing in the appeal letter that the member had reached a functional plateau. By mechanically denying the request because the member completed 5 weeks instead of the plan's required 6 weeks, the plan violated CIC § 10169.5. The plan was legally required to evaluate the treating physician's declaration of a functional plateau rather than mechanically enforcing its internal 6-week rule.

V. CLINICAL EVIDENCE AND GENERALLY ACCEPTED STANDARDS
Generally accepted clinical standards, including the North American Spine Society (NASS) Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020) and the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023), support conservative management as the initial treatment for cervical radiculopathy. However, these guidelines also recognize that when a patient exhibits objective neurological deficits (such as right C7 dermatomal numbness, a diminished tricep reflex, and a 4+/5 grip strength deficit) and has failed to improve after a substantial course of physical therapy and multi-agent pharmacotherapy, surgical decompression via ACDF is a standard and effective treatment option.
Furthermore, clinical standards dictate that forcing a patient who has already reached a functional plateau to undergo additional physical therapy is clinically inappropriate, as it delays necessary definitive care and exposes the patient to prolonged neurological compromise. This clinical consensus is codified in California law under CIC § 10169.5, which recognizes that a documented functional plateau supersedes arbitrary, mechanical duration requirements.

VI. RESOLUTION OF CROSS-SOURCE CONFLICTS
A conflict exists between the plan's internal clinical criteria (CC-SPINE-2024), which require 6 weeks of physical therapy, 4 weeks of two separate medications, and an interventional procedure, and California statutory law (CHSC § 1374.31 and CIC § 10169.5), which invalidates verbal-only denials and prohibits the mechanical application of physical therapy duration requirements when a functional plateau is documented.
Applying the established hierarchy of authority, California statutory law and Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) regulations strictly supersede the plan's internal clinical coverage criteria. The plan cannot rely on clinical non-compliance with its internal criteria to sustain a denial that was issued through a legally defective process and in violation of statutory protections. Because the denial notice is legally defective under CHSC § 1374.31(b), it must be treated as if no denial was issued, and the plan's mechanical enforcement of the 6-week physical therapy requirement is legally impermissible under CIC § 10169.5.

VII. ORDER OF REMAND AND INSTRUCTIONS TO THE PLAN
Based on the foregoing findings, HealthFirst Health Plan is hereby ORDERED to:
1. Vacate the defective initial denial dated October 15, 2024.
2. Re-evaluate the prior authorization request for a single-level ACDF C6-C7 (CPT 22551) for Jessica Turner.
3. In conducting this re-evaluation, the plan must:
   - Apply CIC § 10169.5 and evaluate the treating physician's written declaration of a functional plateau, rather than mechanically enforcing the 6-week physical therapy requirement of CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2(a).
   - Evaluate whether the member's objective neurological deficits (diminished tricep reflex, 4+/5 grip strength) and failed conservative trials (3 months of Meloxicam, 2 weeks of Prednisone, and 5 weeks of PT) establish medical necessity under generally accepted clinical standards.
4. Within five (5) business days of the date of this order, the plan must issue a new determination. If the plan determines that the request is approved, it must issue an authorization. If the plan determines that the request is denied, it must issue a fully compliant, written denial notice that:
   - Explicitly details the specific clinical criteria applied and the specific clinical reasons for the denial.
   - Includes the mandatory written notice of Independent Medical Review (IMR) rights as required by CHSC § 1374.31(a).
   - Is provided in writing to both the member and the treating physician, Dr. Robert Chen.

Failure to issue a compliant written decision within the statutory timeframe may result in the request being deemed approved pursuant to CHSC § 1367.01 and CCR Title 28 § 1300.67.2.1.
ground_truth_answer: REMAND — The clinical denial may be substantively correct (5 weeks PT vs 6 required, no injection, plateau not formally documented in PT records). However, CHSC 1374.31(b) requires written criteria in the denial notice. Verbal peer-to-peer communication cannot substitute for written notice. Plan must reissue a compliant written denial.
genuine_tension: Clinical criteria not met on the merits — 5 weeks PT, no injection, plateau not formally documented. The denial is substantively defensible. But the procedural violation (criteria communicated verbally only, no IMR notice) independently requires remedy.
