HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN
APPEALS AND GRIEVANCES DEPARTMENT
P.O. Box 9000
San Francisco, CA 94120

Date: October 24, 2024

CASE IDENTIFICATION:
- Case ID: PA-2024-D001
- Member Name: Sandra White
- Member ID: M-334466
- Plan Type: HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
- Requesting Provider: Dr. Paul Lee, MD — Neurosurgery (UCLA Medical Center)
- Requested Procedure: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7, single level (CPT 22551)
- Original Denial Date: October 5, 2024
- Appeal Filing Date: October 18, 2024

FINAL APPEAL DISPOSITION: OVERTURNED (DEEMED APPROVED)

Dear Ms. White and Dr. Lee,

The HealthFirst Health Plan Appeals and Grievances Department has completed its review of the first-level internal appeal regarding the prior authorization request for a single-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C6-C7 (CPT 22551). 

After evaluating the clinical records, the plan's internal coverage criteria, and the applicable California regulatory framework, HealthFirst has determined that the initial prior authorization denial dated October 5, 2024, must be OVERTURNED. The requested surgical procedure is hereby DEEMED APPROVED. 

This determination is based on two independent, legally binding grounds under California law: (1) a procedural defect in the initial denial notice that triggers a statutory deemed approval, and (2) a substantive statutory waiver of the plan's physical therapy requirements due to documented objective structural neurological compromise.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. PROCEDURAL ANALYSIS & STATUTORY DEEMED APPROVAL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Under California Health and Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(a), when a health plan issues a prior authorization denial based on medical necessity, it is mandated to provide a written notice that specifies the exact clinical criteria applied, the specific clinical reasons for the denial, and a clear notice of the member's right to an Independent Medical Review (IMR).

The initial denial notice issued by HealthFirst on October 5, 2024, failed to meet these statutory standards. Specifically:
1. The notice did not cite the specific clinical criteria applied, providing only a generic reference to "plan criteria" without a section number or specific criterion text.
2. The notice failed to include the mandatory IMR rights notice.

Under CHSC § 1374.31(b), a denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason for the denial is legally "defective and shall be treated as if no denial was issued for purposes of appeal timelines."

Because the October 5, 2024 notice is legally treated as if no denial was issued, HealthFirst failed to issue a valid decision within the mandatory 5-business-day decision timeframe for standard prior authorizations under CHSC § 1367.01 and California Code of Regulations (CCR) Title 28 § 1300.67.2.1. 

Under CHSC § 1367.01 (Part IV.3 of the California Regulatory Framework), if a plan fails to issue a timely, legally compliant decision within the required timeframe, the request is subject to a mandatory "DEEMED APPROVAL" for the period of the delay. Consequently, because the plan's procedural defects invalidated the initial denial, the surgery is deemed approved by operation of law.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. SUBSTANTIVE CLINICAL ANALYSIS & STATUTORY PT WAIVER
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The plan's initial denial was substantively based on the member's failure to complete the 6-week physical therapy (PT) requirement outlined in HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2(a). The clinical record indicates that the member completed 4 weeks (12 sessions) of supervised PT.

However, the clinical record also documents that the member has objective structural neurological compromise. Specifically:
1. An MRI dated August 15, 2024, demonstrates a C6-C7 disc herniation with moderate right C7 nerve root compression.
2. A neurological examination dated August 20, 2024, documents objective motor weakness (right tricep strength graded at 4/5), right C7 dermatomal numbness, and a diminished right tricep reflex.

Under California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(3), a health insurer is legally prohibited from conditioning the approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy where "the condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address." Furthermore, CIC § 10169.5(c) explicitly prohibits plans from mechanically applying internal requirements for a minimum number of weeks of physical therapy without reference to whether the condition involves neurological urgency under subdivision (a)(3).

Because Ms. White's clinical presentation involves objective structural neurological compromise (moderate C7 nerve root compression with corresponding 4/5 tricep motor weakness and diminished reflex), the plan's internal 6-week PT requirement is legally waived under CIC § 10169.5(a)(3). The mechanical application of the 6-week PT requirement to deny this request was substantively invalid under California law.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. CONCLUSION AND AUTHORIZATION DETAILS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Because the initial denial notice was procedurally defective under CHSC § 1374.31(b), triggering a statutory deemed approval under CHSC § 1367.01, and because the clinical basis for the denial violated the physical therapy waiver mandates of CIC § 10169.5(a)(3), the denial is OVERTURNED.

Authorization details are as follows:
- Approved Procedure: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF), C6-C7, single level
- CPT Code: 22551
- Facility: UCLA Medical Center
- Provider: Dr. Paul Lee, MD
- Authorization Period: Valid for 90 days from the date of this letter (expires January 22, 2025)

If you have any questions regarding this determination, please contact the Appeals and Grievances Department at (800) 555-0199.

Sincerely,

Appeals and Grievances Department
HealthFirst Health Plan
ground_truth_answer: REMAND — The clinical denial is substantively correct (criteria not met: 4 weeks PT vs 6 required, one pharmacotherapy agent, no injection). However, the denial notice violates CHSC 1374.31(b): no specific criteria cited, no section number, no IMR notice. The plan must reissue a compliant denial notice before the member can meaningfully exercise appeal rights.
genuine_tension: Clinical criteria clearly not met — this is a legitimate denial on the merits. But the denial notice violates CHSC 1374.31(b) on multiple grounds. A single-pass system reads the clinical record and upholds. A system applying the full regulatory framework catches the procedural defect. The correct disposition is not a binary overturn/uphold — it is a remand requiring a compliant denial notice.

determination:
**HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN — PRIOR AUTHORIZATION APPEAL DETERMINATION**

**Case ID:** PA-2024-E002
**Member:** Catherine Mills (M-778811), Age 53
**Plan:** HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441, California
**Procedure:** ACDF C3-C4, C4-C5, C5-C6 (three levels)
**Requesting Provider:** Dr. James Torres, MD (Neurosurgery)
**Initial Denial Date:** 2024-11-25
**Review Level:** First-Level Appeal
**Appeal Reviewer:** [Your Name/Title, e.g., Chief Medical Appeals Officer]
**Date of Review:** [Current Date]

---

**I. SUMMARY OF REQUEST AND DENIAL**

Catherine Mills, a 53-year-old member, requested prior authorization for a three-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C3-C4, C4-C5, and C5-C6 for multi-level cervical spondylosis with myeloradiculopathy.

HealthFirst Health Plan initially denied the request for the C3-C4 and C5-C6 levels (Reason Code MED-003), stating that "Review of imaging and clinical record supports surgical intervention at one level (C4-C5) only. C3-C4 and C5-C6 do not demonstrate pathology of sufficient severity to warrant surgical intervention at this time." The denial implicitly approved the C4-C5 level.

The member's appeal asserts that all three levels are symptomatic, the treating surgeon has documented reasoning for a three-level fusion, and conservative treatment has been completed for all levels.

---

**II. REVIEWER'S ROLE AND HIERARCHY OF AUTHORITY**

As an expert health plan appeals reviewer, I have reviewed the clinical record, the plan's clinical coverage criteria (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024), relevant California regulatory frameworks (CIC, CHSC, DMHC APL 22-014), and generally accepted clinical standards of medical practice (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021).

In evaluating this appeal, the following hierarchy of authority has been applied:
1.  **State Law** (California Insurance Code, California Health & Safety Code, DMHC All-Plan Letters)
2.  **Clinical Standard** (Generally Accepted Standards of Medical Practice from recognized professional organizations)
3.  **Plan Criteria** (HealthFirst's internal Clinical Coverage Criteria)

Where conflicts arise between these sources, the higher authority governs.

---

**III. CLINICAL SUMMARY OF MEMBER**

Ms. Mills presents with multi-level cervical spondylosis with myeloradiculopathy.

*   **Presenting Symptoms:** Bilateral hyperreflexia, bilateral Hoffman sign, wide-based gait (myelopathy findings); bilateral deltoid weakness (C5 level) 4/5; left bicep weakness (C6 level) 4-/5, diminished left bicep reflex; neck pain with C3-C4 palpation.
*   **Imaging (MRI 2024-10-01):**
    *   **C4-C5:** Large disc herniation, severe cord compression, T2 signal change (myelomalacia).
    *   **C5-C6:** Moderate disc herniation, moderate left C6 nerve root compression, foraminal stenosis.
    *   **C3-C4:** Mild disc bulge, minimal foraminal narrowing.
*   **Conservative Treatment:**
    *   **Physical Therapy:** 9 weeks (27 sessions). Myelopathic symptoms stable but not improved. C5-C6 radicular symptoms persist. C3-C4 contribution unclear.
    *   **Pharmacotherapy:** Baclofen 10mg TID for 3 months (minimal spasticity relief); Pregabalin 300mg BID for 4 months (partial pain relief).
    *   **Interventional:** Cervical epidural steroid injection on 2024-10-20 (modest improvement in radicular symptoms, no change in myelopathy signs).

---

**IV. DETAILED REVIEW AND ANALYSIS**

**A. Procedural Adequacy of Denial Notice (CHSC § 1374.31(b))**
The initial denial notice specified "MED-003" and provided a clinical reason (insufficient pathology for C3-C4 and C5-C6). While it did not explicitly cite the plan's criteria document or detail IMR rights, the reason provided is sufficiently specific to allow for appeal. Thus, the denial is considered procedurally adequate for the purpose of this review.

**B. Application of Plan Criteria (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024)**

1.  **Diagnosis Requirement (2.1):** The member clearly meets criteria for cervical myelopathy (2.1b) at C4-C5 and cervical radiculopathy (2.1a) at C5-C6, with objective neurological deficits (2.1c) and supporting MRI within 6 months. This criterion is satisfied for C4-C5 and C5-C6.
2.  **Conservative Treatment Requirement (2.2):**
    *   The member completed 9 weeks of PT (exceeding the standard 6 weeks), 3-4 months of two pharmacotherapy agents (exceeding the 4-week minimum), and one interventional procedure.
    *   **Myelopathy Exception (2.2A):** Given the clear evidence of moderate-severe cervical myelopathy with myelomalacia and upper motor neuron signs at C4-C5, myelopathy is a primary diagnosis. The plan's exception should apply, reducing PT to 4 weeks (met) and waiving interventional treatment if physician documents risk (not documented, but interventional treatment was pursued anyway). The pharmacotherapy requirement (met) remains. The member's conservative treatment exceeds the requirements of the myelopathy exception.
    *   Therefore, the conservative treatment requirements under the plan's criteria, including the myelopathy exception, have been met for the primary condition.
3.  **Imaging Requirement (2.3) and Pathology Severity (Denial Reason 3.3):**
    *   **C4-C5:** The MRI demonstrates severe cord compression and myelomalacia, fully consistent with myelopathy. This level was implicitly approved by the plan, and is medically necessary.
    *   **C5-C6:** The MRI shows moderate disc herniation, moderate left C6 nerve root compression, and foraminal stenosis. This is consistent with the left C6 weakness and diminished reflex on exam and persistent radicular symptoms. The plan's denial based on "insufficient severity" for this level is reviewed against clinical standards.
    *   **C3-C4:** The MRI shows mild disc bulge and minimal foraminal narrowing. The neurological exam notes neck pain but no specific radicular pattern at this level. The plan's denial for "insufficient severity" for this level is reviewed against clinical standards.

**C. Application of California Regulatory Requirements (State Law)**

1.  **DMHC All-Plan Letter APL 22-014 (Myelopathy and Urgent Conditions):**
    *   **II.1 Myelopathy Classification:** The member has myelopathy with objective cord compression and myelomalacia at C4-C5. DMHC mandates such cases be treated as urgent due to potential for irreversible harm.
    *   **II.2 Conservative Treatment Exceptions:** For conditions risking irreversible harm (like myelopathy with myelomalacia), plans SHALL NOT require full conservative treatment when objective imaging shows progressive pathology (myelomalacia indicates existing cord injury/progressive risk), treating physician documents conservative failure (PT notes: "Myelopathic symptoms stable but not improved. C5-C6 radicular symptoms persist"), and surgery is indicated under generally accepted guidelines. Myelomalacia specifically supports waiver of standard conservative requirements.
    *   **II.3 Plan Criteria vs. Clinical Standard:** Plans shall not apply internal criteria more restrictive than generally accepted standards.

2.  **CIC § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy as Prerequisite):**
    *   **(a)(3) Objective evidence of structural neurological compromise:** At C4-C5, severe cord compression with myelomalacia constitutes structural neurological compromise that PT cannot address. At C5-C6, moderate nerve root compression with objective C6 weakness also falls under this.
    *   **(a)(2) Functional plateau:** The member completed 9 weeks of PT, and symptoms for both myelopathy and C5-C6 radiculopathy persisted/did not improve. This constitutes reaching a functional plateau, as defined clinically (less than 10% improvement or therapist documented maximum benefit).
    *   This state law overrides any plan requirement for a minimum number of weeks of PT in this specific clinical scenario, as the member has either reached a functional plateau or has objective neurological compromise.

3.  **CHSC § 1374.32(b) (IMR Standard is NOT plan criteria):** This critical provision mandates that if a service meets generally accepted standards of medical practice, it SHALL be approved, regardless of whether the plan's internal criteria are more restrictive.

**D. Application of Clinical Standard (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021)**

1.  **Myelopathy (C4-C5):** The member has confirmed moderate-severe cervical myelopathy (bilateral UMN signs, gait disturbance, severe cord compression, myelomalacia).
    *   AANS/CNS 2023 (Section 3.1) considers myelomalacia on MRI and moderate-severe myelopathy with objective cord compression as TIER 1 strong surgical indications.
    *   AO Spine 2021 (Section 2.1) explicitly states no high-quality evidence supports mandatory PT before surgery for moderate-severe myelopathy, and delaying surgery may result in deterioration.
    *   The plan's implicit approval of C4-C5 aligns with these strong clinical standards.

2.  **Radiculopathy (C5-C6):** The member has objective C6 nerve root compression, C6 weakness, and persistent radicular symptoms after 9 weeks of PT, 4 months of pharmacotherapy, and an epidural.
    *   AANS/CNS 2023 (Section 3.1) categorizes radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks of conservative treatment as a TIER 2 reasonable surgical indication. The member has exceeded the duration for conservative treatment, and symptoms persist.
    *   The plan's denial based on "insufficient severity" for C5-C6 is more restrictive than generally accepted clinical standards when objective neurological deficits and failed conservative treatment are present, especially in the context of adjacent myelopathy.

3.  **C3-C4:** The MRI shows only mild disc bulge and minimal foraminal narrowing, and the neurological exam notes neck pain but no specific radicular pattern or myelopathy attributable to this level.
    *   AANS/CNS 2023 (Section 3.1) considers imaging findings without correlating symptoms as a TIER 3 (surgery not indicated) scenario. Surgery for axial neck pain alone without radiculopathy or myelopathy is also not indicated.
    *   For this level, the plan's denial based on "insufficient severity" aligns with generally accepted clinical standards.

---

**V. CROSS-SOURCE CONFLICT RESOLUTION**

*   **For C4-C5 (Myelopathy):** The plan's implicit approval is consistent with State Law (DMHC APL 22-014, CIC 10169.5) and Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS TIER 1). No conflict.
*   **For C5-C6 (Radiculopathy):** The plan's denial for "insufficient severity" conflicts with both State Law and Clinical Standards.
    *   **State Law:** CIC 10169.5 mandates waiver of PT requirements due to functional plateau and neurological compromise. DMHC APL 22-014 prohibits plans from applying criteria more restrictive than generally accepted standards.
    *   **Clinical Standards:** AANS/CNS considers persistent radiculopathy with neurological deficit after adequate conservative treatment (met here) a reasonable surgical indication. The presence of moderate disc herniation, nerve root compression, and weakness with persistent symptoms is not "insufficient severity" by generally accepted standards.
    *   **Resolution:** State law and clinical standards override the plan's restrictive interpretation. Surgical intervention for C5-C6 is medically necessary.
*   **For C3-C4:** The plan's denial for "insufficient severity" aligns with Clinical Standards, which do not support surgery for mild imaging findings without correlating neurological symptoms. No conflict.

---

**VI. FINAL DETERMINATION**

**DISPOSITION: PARTIAL OVERTURN**

The prior authorization denial for procedure code 22551 (ACDF) for Catherine Mills is **PARTIALLY OVERTURNED**.

*   Authorization for **ACDF at C4-C5 and C5-C6** is **APPROVED**.
*   Authorization for **ACDF at C3-C4** is **UPHELD** (DENIED).

---

**VII. WARRANT FOR DETERMINATION**

1.  **C4-C5 (Myelopathy) — APPROVED:** The member has clear, objective evidence of moderate-to-severe cervical myelopathy at C4-C5, including severe cord compression and myelomalacia on MRI, with corresponding upper motor neuron signs (bilateral hyperreflexia, Hoffman, gait disturbance) and bilateral C5 weakness. Per **AANS/CNS 2023 Guidelines (Section 3.1)**, myelomalacia and moderate-to-severe myelopathy are TIER 1 strong surgical indications. **DMHC APL 22-014 (II.1 & II.2)** explicitly identifies such myelopathy with myelomalacia as an urgent condition warranting surgical intervention without requiring a full course of conservative treatment. The plan implicitly approved this level, which is consistent with all applicable standards.

2.  **C5-C6 (Radiculopathy) — APPROVED:** The member demonstrates objective evidence of C6 nerve root compression, moderate disc herniation, left C6 weakness (4-/5), and diminished left bicep reflex. She has completed an extensive course of conservative treatment, including 9 weeks of physical therapy, 4 months of pharmacotherapy, and an epidural, with persistent radicular symptoms ("C5-C6 radicular symptoms persist"). This satisfies the definition of a functional plateau and failed conservative management for radiculopathy (**CIC § 10169.5(a)(2) & (b)** and **Clinical Standard Section 5**). **AANS/CNS 2023 Guidelines (Section 3.1)** consider persistent radiculopathy with symptoms after 6-12 weeks of conservative treatment a TIER 2 reasonable surgical indication. The plan's denial based on "insufficient severity" is more restrictive than these generally accepted standards and is overridden by **CHSC § 1374.32(b)** and **DMHC APL 22-014 (II.3)**.

3.  **C3-C4 — UPHELD (DENIED):** The imaging for C3-C4 shows only mild disc bulge and minimal foraminal narrowing. The neurological exam notes neck pain but no specific radicular pattern or myelopathic signs attributable to this level. Per **AANS/CNS 2023 Guidelines (Section 3.1, TIER 3)**, surgery is not indicated for imaging findings without correlating symptoms or for axial neck pain alone. The plan's denial based on "insufficient severity" for this level is consistent with generally accepted clinical standards.

Therefore, surgical intervention is medically necessary for decompression and fusion at the C4-C5 and C5-C6 levels but not at C3-C4.

(2) C5-C6: OVERTURN based on moderate compression, documented C6 neurological deficit, and met conservative treatment criteria. (3) C3-C4: UPHOLD — mild imaging findings, no specific radicular pattern documented, insufficient basis for surgical authorization at this level.

## HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN — PRIOR AUTHORIZATION APPEAL DETERMINATION

**Case ID:** PA-2024-E003
**Member Name:** George Harris
**Member ID:** M-889922
**Procedure:** CPT 22551 (Revision ACDF C5-C6)
**Date of Denial:** 2024-10-30
**Reviewer:** Appeals Reviewer, HealthFirst Medical Department
**Date of Review:** 2024-11-20

---

### **1. OVERVIEW**

This appeal concerns a prior authorization request for a revision anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 for Mr. George Harris, a 48-year-old member with HealthFirst PPO Gold. The initial request for CPT 22551 was denied by Dr. Patricia Huang on 2024-10-30 with Reason Code MED-003, stating: "Revision surgery not covered under standard ACDF criteria. Member had prior C5-C6 ACDF in 2021. Revision criteria require documentation of hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, or new pathology at previously treated level. Documentation submitted does not confirm hardware failure."

The appeal basis provided by the treating surgeon, Dr. Karen Williams, states: "CT scan confirms pseudarthrosis (failure of fusion) at C5-C6," "Symptoms have returned and worsened since 2021 fusion," and "Revision criteria met per treating surgeon."

### **2. CLINICAL FINDINGS AND ASSESSMENT**

**Presenting Diagnosis:** Pseudarthrosis C5-C6 following prior ACDF 2021 — failed fusion, causing symptomatic cervical radiculopathy.

**Key Clinical Information:**
*   **Prior Surgery:** C5-C6 ACDF in 2021, with symptoms recurring at 18 months.
*   **Current Symptoms:** Return of right C6 symptoms including bicep weakness (4/5 right), diminished bicep reflex (right), and C6 dermatomal numbness, noted to be *worse than preoperative baseline* (Neurological Exam, 2024-09-20). These findings are consistent with cervical radiculopathy. No documented myelopathic signs (e.g., bilateral weakness, gait disturbance, hyperreflexia, Hoffman sign).
*   **Imaging:**
    *   MRI (2024-09-01): Limited by hardware artifact; possible non-union, cannot confirm.
    *   CT (2024-09-15): "CT without artifact limitation: C5-C6 — incomplete bridging bone formation. Lucency around hardware suggesting pseudarthrosis. Findings consistent with failed fusion/pseudarthrosis. Hardware appears intact without fracture."
*   **Conservative Treatment:**
    *   Physical Therapy: 8 weeks (24 sessions) completed. Documented "No improvement." Treating physician notes PT "cannot address structural hardware/fusion failure."
    *   Pharmacotherapy: Naproxen 500mg BID for 4 months (partial pain relief), Gabapentin 300mg TID for 3 months (partial neuropathic relief).
    *   Interventional: Epidural (2024-10-10) with "Minimal improvement — treating physician notes this is expected when structural failure is present."

### **3. REVIEW AGAINST APPLICABLE CRITERIA AND STANDARDS**

This review applies the hierarchy of authority: **State Law > Clinical Standard > Plan Criteria.**

#### **3.1 HealthFirst Plan Clinical Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024)**

*   **Scope (Section 1):** CPT 22551 is explicitly covered.
*   **Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1):** Member has a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy (2.1a) with objective neurological deficit, supported by current CT imaging demonstrating structural pathology (pseudarthrosis at C5-C6) consistent with symptoms. This criterion is met.
*   **Conservative Treatment Requirement (Section 2.2):**
    *   The member completed 8 weeks of supervised PT (minimum 6 weeks required).
    *   The member completed trials of two pharmacotherapy agents (Naproxen for 4 months, Gabapentin for 3 months; minimum 4 weeks each required).
    *   The member received one interventional treatment (epidural).
    *   Based on these facts, the *quantitative* conservative treatment requirements of Section 2.2 appear to have been met.
    *   **Myelopathy Exception (2.2A):** This exception is not applicable as the primary clinical presentation is cervical radiculopathy, not myelopathy, as per the neurological exam provided.
*   **Imaging Requirement (Section 2.3):** Current CT scan (2024-09-15) demonstrates pseudarthrosis at C5-C6, consistent with the member's radicular symptoms. This criterion is met.
*   **Physician Documentation (Section 2.4):** The provided clinical record satisfies the elements of physician documentation.
*   **Exclusions (Section 3):**
    *   **Denial Reason Misapplication:** The initial denial stated: "Revision criteria require documentation of hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, or new pathology at previously treated level. Documentation submitted does not confirm hardware failure." However, the CT scan explicitly confirms **pseudarthrosis** (incomplete bridging bone formation, lucency around hardware), which is one of the *explicitly stated criteria for revision surgery* in the denial reason itself. The initial denial failed to acknowledge or apply its own stated criteria regarding pseudarthrosis. This constitutes a direct misapplication of the plan's criteria.

#### **3.2 California Regulatory Framework**

*   **CHSC § 1374.31(b) (Denial Notice Defect):** The initial denial notice is potentially defective as it failed to specify the "specific clinical reason" for denial by ignoring the documented pseudarthrosis, which was a listed reason for revision in its *own stated criteria*. By solely focusing on "hardware failure" and disregarding "pseudarthrosis," the denial notice did not accurately reflect the clinical situation in light of its stated policy.
*   **CIC § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy as Prerequisite):** This state law explicitly overrides plan requirements for PT completion under certain conditions:
    *   **(a)(1) PT unlikely to benefit:** The treating physician documented that PT "cannot address structural hardware/fusion failure," indicating it is unlikely to benefit the member given the nature of the condition.
    *   **(a)(2) Functional Plateau:** The member completed 8 weeks of PT with "No improvement." This constitutes reaching a functional plateau as per the clinical definition (<10% improvement or maximum benefit reached).
    *   **(a)(3) Objective evidence of structural neurological compromise:** The CT scan confirms pseudarthrosis, causing C6 radiculopathy (bicep weakness, numbness, reflex change). This is objective structural neurological compromise that PT cannot address.
    *   **Conclusion:** Even if the plan were to argue insufficient conservative treatment, CIC § 10169.5 would override any mechanical PT duration requirement.
*   **DMHC APL 22-014 (Conservative Treatment Exceptions):** While primarily focused on myelopathy, Section II.2 outlines conservative treatment exceptions for conditions risking irreversible harm when:
    *   (a) Objective imaging (CT showing pseudarthrosis) demonstrates progressive pathology.
    *   (b) Treating physician documents conservative treatment failure (8 weeks PT, pharmacotherapy, epidural with minimal/no improvement).
    *   (c) Surgical intervention is indicated under generally accepted guidelines.
    *   The current radiculopathy is worsening ("worse than preoperative baseline") due to a structural failure (pseudarthrosis) that conservative measures cannot resolve. This supports waiving further conservative treatment requirements.
*   **CHSC § 1374.32(b) (IMR Standard vs. Plan Criteria):** This is critical. California law mandates that the service shall be approved if it meets generally accepted standards of medical practice, regardless of whether the plan's internal criteria are more restrictive.

#### **3.3 Clinical Standard (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021)**

*   **Diagnostic Classification (Section 1.1):** The symptoms are clearly classified as cervical radiculopathy.
*   **Conservative Treatment for Radiculopathy:** Clinical guidelines generally recommend a trial of conservative treatment (PT, pharmacotherapy, injections) for radiculopathy. The member has undergone a substantial course of conservative treatment (8 weeks PT, 3-4 months pharmacotherapy, 1 epidural) with minimal to no improvement. Crucially, the underlying pathology is structural pseudarthrosis, which is unlikely to resolve with non-surgical management.
*   **Surgical Indications (Section 3.1):** Per AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023):
    *   TIER 2 — REASONABLE INDICATION:
        *   (b) "Radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks conservative tx." Mr. Harris has persistent, worsening C6 radiculopathy after a trial of conservative treatment.
        *   (c) "Significant functional impairment not responding to conservative care." His documented 4/5 bicep weakness and numbness, worsening from baseline, clearly demonstrate significant functional impairment.
    *   **Conclusion:** Surgical intervention (revision ACDF) for symptomatic pseudarthrosis causing persistent radiculopathy after failed conservative treatment is consistent with generally accepted standards of medical practice.

### **4. CONCLUSION**

The initial denial was based on a misapplication of HealthFirst's own stated criteria. The denial asserted that "revision criteria require documentation of hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, or new pathology," but then denied because "documentation submitted does not confirm hardware failure." This selectively ignored the explicit inclusion of "pseudarthrosis" as a valid reason for revision. The CT scan clearly documents pseudarthrosis at C5-C6.

Furthermore, even if conservative treatment completion were a point of contention (which it was not in the original denial), state law (CIC § 10169.5 and DMHC APL 22-014) provides clear exceptions that have been met in this case due to the structural nature of the pathology (pseudarthrosis causing neurological compromise) and documented failure of conservative measures.

Finally, surgical intervention for symptomatic pseudarthrosis causing persistent radiculopathy, particularly with objective neurological deficit and progression, is well-supported by generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS, NASS, AO Spine).

### **5. DISPOSITION**

**OVERTURN**

### **6. WARRANT**

The denial for CPT 22551 (Revision ACDF C5-C6) for Mr. George Harris is hereby OVERTURNED for the following reasons:

1.  **Misapplication of Plan Criteria:** HealthFirst's initial denial incorrectly applied its own criteria by stating that revision surgery criteria include "pseudarthrosis" but then denying the request solely on the absence of "hardware failure," completely disregarding the CT-confirmed pseudarthrosis at C5-C6 (CT 2024-09-15). This represents a direct contradiction and misapplication of the plan's stated policy as articulated in the denial letter itself.
2.  **Compliance with State Law (CIC § 10169.5):** The member has undergone 8 weeks of physical therapy with "No improvement," and the treating physician documented that PT "cannot address structural hardware/fusion failure." This fulfills the conditions of CIC § 10169.5(a)(1), (a)(2), and (a)(3), which mandate that a plan "shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy" when PT is unlikely to benefit, a functional plateau has been reached, or objective structural neurological compromise (pseudarthrosis causing radiculopathy) is present that PT cannot address. Therefore, any requirement for further conservative treatment is overridden by California state law.
3.  **Adherence to Clinical Standards:** Generally accepted clinical guidelines (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021) classify persistent radiculopathy with objective neurological deficits (4/5 weakness, diminished reflex, numbness) caused by structural pathology like pseudarthrosis, after a trial of conservative care, as a reasonable indication for surgical intervention (Tier 2 indication per AANS/CNS). The member's symptoms are worsening ("worse than preoperative baseline"), indicating clinical necessity for surgical correction of the failed fusion.
4.  **Overall Medical Necessity:** The requested revision ACDF is medically necessary to address the documented pseudarthrosis causing persistent and worsening C6 radiculopathy, consistent with prudent clinical judgment and generally accepted standards of medical practice in California.

**The requested prior authorization for CPT 22551 is approved.**

# California Independent Clinical Appeal Determination

### Case Metadata
*   **Case ID:** PA-2024-E002
*   **Member Name:** Catherine Mills
*   **Member ID:** M-778811
*   **Plan Type:** HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
*   **State of Jurisdiction:** California
*   **Disputed Procedure:** Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) — Three Levels (C3-C4, C4-C5, and C5-C6) [CPT Code: 22551]
*   **Requesting Physician:** Dr. James Torres, MD (Neurosurgery)
*   **Facility:** Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
*   **Date of Review:** November 29, 2024

---

### Final Appeal Determination
**DISPOSITION: PARTIAL OVERTURN**

*   **C4-C5 Level:** **OVERTURN** (Medical necessity established; previously approved by plan).
*   **C5-C6 Level:** **OVERTURN** (Medical necessity established; plan denial is reversed. Surgical fusion is authorized at this level).
*   **C3-C4 Level:** **UPHOLD** (Medical necessity not established; plan denial is confirmed. Surgical fusion is not authorized at this level).

**Summary of Approved Procedure:** A **two-level anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at C4-C5 and C5-C6** is authorized as medically necessary under California law and generally accepted clinical standards. The addition of the C3-C4 level is denied.

---

## Detailed Clinical & Legal Evaluation

### Step 1: Procedural Adequacy and Defect Check
Under **California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b)**, any health plan medical necessity denial must specify the exact clinical criteria applied and provide an individualized clinical explanation for the denial of each requested level. 

*   **Procedural Defect Identified:** The HealthFirst initial denial notice dated November 25, 2024, is procedurally defective. While it references a clinical code ("MED-003"), it fails to explicitly cite the plan's governing clinical policy (**HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024**). Furthermore, it groups C3-C4 and C5-C6 together in a single brief statement ("do not demonstrate pathology of sufficient severity") without providing separate, individualized clinical rationales. This lumping constitutes a procedural failure given the vastly different clinical and imaging profiles of these two levels.
*   **Application of Hierarchy of Authority:** Under CHSC § 1374.31(b), a defective denial is treated as if no denial was issued. However, in exercising prudent clinical judgment as mandated by **CHSC § 1374.32(a)**, the reviewer cannot utilize a procedural defect to authorize a clinically inappropriate, invasive surgical fusion at a non-pathological level (C3-C4). Doing so would expose the member to unnecessary surgical risks (e.g., adjacent segment disease, pseudarthrosis) in violation of patient safety standards. Therefore, a substantive clinical and statutory evaluation of each disputed level is executed below to determine clinical medical necessity.

---

### Step 2: Diagnostic and Severity Classification
A rigorous level-by-level clinical and radiographic analysis was conducted using the imaging of October 1, 2024, and the neurological exam of October 5, 2024:

1.  **C4-C5 Level (Myelopathy):**
    *   *Imaging:* Large disc herniation with severe spinal cord compression and T2-weighted cord signal change (myelomalacia).
    *   *Clinical Exam:* Bilateral hyperreflexia, bilateral Hoffman sign, wide-based gait, and bilateral deltoid (C5) weakness (4/5).
    *   *Classification:* **Severe Cervical Myelopathy with Myelomalacia.**
2.  **C5-C6 Level (Radiculopathy):**
    *   *Imaging:* Moderate disc herniation, moderate left C6 nerve root compression, and moderate foraminal stenosis.
    *   *Clinical Exam:* Left bicep (C6) motor weakness (4-/5) and a diminished left bicep reflex.
    *   *Classification:* **Objective Left-Sided C6 Cervical Radiculopathy.**
3.  **C3-C4 Level (Axial Pain Only):**
    *   *Imaging:* Mild disc bulge and minimal foraminal narrowing. No cord compression or myelomalacia.
    *   *Clinical Exam:* No radicular weakness or reflex deficits localizing to this level. Exam notes "unclear — neck pain with C3-C4 palpation but no specific radicular pattern." Physical therapy notes state "C3-C4 contribution unclear."
    *   *Classification:* **Axial Neck Pain without Neurological Compromise.**

---

### Step 3: Application of Plan Clinical Criteria & Myelopathy Exception
The clinical records were evaluated against **HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024**:

*   **C4-C5 Level:** Meets Criterion 2.1(b) (confirmed cervical myelopathy) and triggers **Exception 2.2(A) (Myelopathy Pathway)**. Standard interventional therapy requirements are waived due to the risk of neurological deterioration associated with severe cord compression. PT was completed, and pharmacotherapy was trialed (Baclofen 3 months, Pregabalin 4 months). This level is approved.
*   **C5-C6 Level:** Meets standard **Section 2 Medical Necessity Criteria**. 
    *   *Criterion 2.1(a) (Radiculopathy):* Satisfied by moderate left C6 nerve root compression correlating with documented left bicep weakness (4-/5) and a diminished left bicep reflex.
    *   *Criterion 2.2 (Conservative Treatment):* Fully completed. The member completed 9 weeks (27 sessions) of supervised physical therapy (exceeding the 6-week requirement). The PT notes confirm a functional plateau ("radicular symptoms persist"). The member trialed two neuropathic/muscle relaxant medications (Baclofen 10mg TID for 3 months and Pregabalin 300mg BID for 4 months, satisfying the 4-week requirement). The member also underwent a cervical epidural steroid injection on October 20, 2024, with only "modest improvement" in radicular symptoms.
    *   *Conclusion:* The plan's initial denial of C5-C6 on the basis of "insufficient severity" directly contradicts its own policy criteria. The member meets every standard requirement for C5-C6 decompression and fusion.
*   **C3-C4 Level:** Fails to meet Section 2 criteria. Under **Section 3.1 (Exclusions)**, surgery is explicitly excluded when requested solely for axial neck pain without documented radiculopathy or myelopathy. The clinical record demonstrates only localized tenderness and mild, non-compressive bulging at C3-C4, with no correlating neurological deficits.

---

### Step 4: Statutory Override Analysis (California Law)
Where plan criteria are applied restrictively to deny necessary care, California statutory authority overrides plan policies:

*   **CIC § 10169.5 & DMHC All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014:** These regulations mandate that health plans shall not condition surgical approval on conservative therapy (like physical therapy) when:
    1.  Objective imaging shows structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address (such as cord compression and myelomalacia).
    2.  The member has completed physical therapy and reached a documented functional plateau.
*   **Application to C4-C5:** The presence of severe spinal cord compression and myelomalacia (T2 cord signal change) on MRI represents irreversible structural injury. Conditioning surgical decompression on continued physical therapy is legally prohibited under **CIC § 10169.5(a)(3)** and **APL 22-014**.
*   **Application to C5-C6:** The member completed 9 weeks (27 sessions) of physical therapy and reached a documented clinical plateau, with persisting left-sided bicep weakness and radicular symptoms. Insisting on further conservative trials or denying authorization for this level violates **CIC § 10169.5(a)(2)**.
*   **Application to C3-C4:** There is no objective structural compromise, myelomalacia, or nerve root compression at this level. No statutory override applies.

---

### Step 5: Clinical Standards / Independent Medical Review (IMR) Evaluation
As mandated by **CHSC § 1374.32(b)**, the final standard for medical necessity in a California appeal is determined by generally accepted standards of medical practice (**AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines 2023** and **AO Spine Guidelines 2021**), which supersede restrictive plan criteria:

*   **C4-C5 (Myelopathy with Myelomalacia):** Classified under **AANS/CNS Tier 1 (Strong Surgical Indication)**. Delaying surgical decompression to pursue further conservative treatment in the presence of myelomalacia is a clinical error that risks irreversible spinal cord injury, including permanent quadriplegia or bowel/bladder dysfunction.
*   **C5-C6 (Symptomatic Radiculopathy):** Classified under **AANS/CNS Tier 2 (Surgical Indication)**. The member has objective motor weakness (left biceps 4-/5) and reflex loss that has failed 9 weeks of physical therapy, dual-agent pharmacotherapy, and interventional epidural injection. Performing a C4-C5 fusion while leaving an adjacent, highly symptomatic C5-C6 radiculopathy untreated is clinically contraindicated. It would leave the patient's active motor deficit unaddressed and subject the C5-C6 level to accelerated adjacent segment degeneration, requiring a subsequent revision surgery. Fusing C5-C6 concurrently is the standard of care.
*   **C3-C4 (Axial Neck Pain / Non-Specific Pathology):** Classified under **AANS/CNS Tier 3 (Surgery Not Indicated)**. Fusing a segment with mild bulging and localized palpation tenderness—without radicular or myelopathic findings—is not supported by clinical evidence. Extending a multi-level fusion to C3-C4 unnecessarily restricts cervical range of motion and increases the risk of pseudarthrosis and adjacent segment disease at C2-C3, without clinical benefit.

---

### Conclusion of Medical Necessity
A three-level ACDF is **partially medically necessary**.
*   The clinical evidence, California statutes (**CIC § 10169.5**, **APL 22-014**), and professional guidelines (**AANS/CNS 2023**, **AO Spine 2021**) support the medical necessity of a **two-level ACDF at C4-C5 and C5-C6** to treat severe myelopathy with myelomalacia and symptomatic C6 radiculopathy with objective motor weakness.
*   The addition of the **C3-C4** level is not medically necessary and is clinically excluded.

The health plan's initial denial of C5-C6 is **OVERTURNED**. The health plan's denial of C3-C4 is **UPHELD**.

(2) C5-C6: OVERTURN based on moderate compression, documented C6 neurological deficit, and met conservative treatment criteria. (3) C3-C4: UPHOLD — mild imaging findings, no specific radicular pattern documented, insufficient basis for surgical authorization at this level.

The plan's binary denial gets the aggregate wrong even if it got one level right.

# FORMAL APPEAL DETERMINATION

**CASE ID:** PA-2024-E003  
**MEMBER:** George Harris (ID: M-889922)  
**AGE:** 48  
**PLAN:** HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441  
**STATE:** California (Plan Year: 2024 | Coverage Effective: 2021-01-01)  
**REQUESTED PROCEDURE:** CPT 22551 — Revision Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6  
**REQUESTING PROVIDER:** Dr. Karen Williams, MD — Revision Spine Surgery  
**FACILITY:** UCSF Medical Center  
**INITIAL DENIAL DATE:** October 30, 2024  
**INITIAL REVIEWER:** Dr. Patricia Huang, MD  
**DISPOSITION:** **OVERTURNED** (Surgical Authorization Mandated Immediately)  

---

### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
This is a formal appeal review of the medical necessity denial issued on October 30, 2024, by HealthFirst Health Plan for a requested revision anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 (CPT 22551) at UCSF Medical Center. The plan's initial denial asserted that revision surgery was not covered because the submitted documentation did not confirm "hardware failure" under standard ACDF criteria. 

Following a exhaustive review of the clinical record, active plan guidelines, California statutory mandates, and national neurosurgical standards, **the initial denial is OVERTURNED**. 

The plan’s denial is both **procedurally defective** and **clinically invalid**. The member has documented, symptomatic pseudarthrosis (failed fusion) with objective, progressive neurological deficits (right C6 radiculopathy with 4/5 bicep weakness and diminished reflex) that have failed to respond to an extensive, fully completed course of conservative therapy. Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32(b), California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5, and generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS 2023, AO Spine 2021), this procedure is medically necessary and must be approved.

---

### DETAILED STEP-BY-STEP EVALUATION

#### Step 1: Procedural Adequacy and Regulatory Defect Review (CHSC § 1374.31(b))
The initial denial notice issued by Dr. Patricia Huang, MD on October 30, 2024, was evaluated to determine compliance with California statutory disclosure requirements.
* **Finding:** **Procedurally Defective.** 
* **Analysis:** Under **CHSC § 1374.31(b)**, a health plan's denial notice is legally defective if it applies restrictive criteria that are not documented or defined within the active clinical coverage policy, or if it fails to provide a sound clinical basis for its determination. 
The active plan policy, **HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024**, contains no separate "Revision criteria" and does not restrict revision coverage solely to cases demonstrating physical "hardware fracture." The denial letter applied a highly restrictive, unwritten "hardware failure only" rule, while simultaneously ignoring the CT-confirmed pseudarthrosis. Under **CHSC § 1374.31(b)**, a procedurally defective notice is treated as if no denial was issued, triggering a procedural overturn.

#### Step 2: Clinical Presentation and Pathology Verification
The clinical notes and advanced imaging from within the preceding six months were analyzed to establish the diagnosis and pathological severity.
* **Finding:** The clinical record confirms **symptomatic, structural pseudarthrosis (failed fusion) of the C5-C6 level with objective right C6 radiculopathy**.
* **Clinical Evidence:** 
  * **Symptomatology:** Return and worsening of severe right C6 radicular symptoms since the 2021 index surgery, worse than the preoperative baseline.
  * **Neurological Exam (2024-09-20):** Objective right C6 motor deficit (bicep weakness graded 4/5), diminished right bicep reflex, and C6 dermatomal numbness.
  * **Advanced Imaging (CT Scan, 2024-09-15):** Complete CT scan without hardware artifact limits demonstrating incomplete bridging bone formation and lucency around the hardware. The findings are highly diagnostic of pseudarthrosis (failed fusion). Although the metallic hardware is physically intact (unfractured), the biological fusion has failed, resulting in structural instability and nerve root compression.

#### Step 3: Application of Plan Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024)
The clinical record was evaluated against HealthFirst's active internal guidelines (**CC-SPINE-2024**).
* **Finding:** **All standard medical necessity criteria are met in full.**
* **Analysis:**
  * **Section 2.1 (Diagnosis):** The member has confirmed cervical radiculopathy (2.1(a)) with objective neurological deficits (4/5 bicep weakness, diminished reflex, C6 dermatomal numbness) and correlating imaging (2.3).
  * **Section 2.2 (Conservative Treatment):** The plan's standard conservative requirements are fully satisfied:
    * *(a) Physical Therapy:* The member completed **8 weeks (24 sessions)** of supervised physical therapy, exceeding the 6-week minimum. The treating physician documented a functional plateau, noting that physical therapy cannot address a structural, mechanical non-union.
    * *(b) Pharmacotherapy:* The member completed a trial of two agents for $>4$ weeks: Naproxen 500mg BID (4 months) and Gabapentin 300mg TID (3 months).
    * *(c) Interventional Treatment:* The member underwent a cervical epidural steroid injection on October 10, 2024, with minimal improvement.
  * **Conclusion:** The initial reviewer’s assertion that the member failed to meet criteria is factually incorrect. The member satisfied every conservative and diagnostic prerequisite outlined in CC-SPINE-2024.

#### Step 4: Statutory Physical Therapy and Conservative Treatment Override Analysis (CIC § 10169.5)
The application of California statutory protections was assessed to determine if the plan's conservative therapy requirements are legally waived or overridden.
* **Finding:** **State law overrides the plan's restrictive application.**
* **Analysis:** Under **CIC § 10169.5(a)(2)**, a health plan cannot mechanically enforce conservative therapy timelines when a member has completed a course of physical therapy and reached a documented **functional plateau** without symptom resolution. 
* Under **CIC § 10169.5(a)(3)**, conservative requirements are waived when there is objective evidence of structural compromise that physical therapy cannot address. Pseudarthrosis (failed biological fusion) with lucency around hardware is a mechanical, structural failure. Physical therapy cannot regenerate bridging bone or stabilize a loose construct. Denying surgical correction based on conservative failure in this setting violates California insurance law.

#### Step 5: Generally Accepted Clinical Standards Evaluation (AANS/CNS 2023, AO Spine 2021)
The clinical scenario was reviewed under national neurosurgical and orthopedic guidelines, which supersede internal health plan policies under California law (**CHSC § 1374.32(b)**).
* **Finding:** The requested revision surgery is **strongly indicated and medically necessary** under generally accepted standards.
* **Neurosurgical Standards:** 
  * **AANS/CNS 2023 Guidelines:** Revision surgery is a **Tier 1 (Strongly Indicated)** recommendation for patients with symptomatic pseudarthrosis (failed fusion) accompanied by objective neurological deficits (motor weakness, reflex changes) who have failed conservative treatment. 
  * **AO Spine 2021 Guidelines:** It is clinically contraindicated to delay surgical stabilization and decompression in patients with progressive radicular motor deficits (4/5 weakness) and mechanical pseudarthrosis. Mandating further conservative treatment for a structural non-union risks permanent, irreversible neurological injury.

---

### DISPOSITION DECISION
Following the strict **Source Hierarchy of Authority** ($\text{California Law} > \text{Clinical Standards} > \text{Plan Criteria}$):

1. **Procedural Path:** The initial denial was procedurally defective under **CHSC § 1374.31(b)** by applying "Revision criteria" not present in the plan's policy, requiring an immediate procedural overturn.
2. **Substantive Plan Path:** The clinical record demonstrates that the member met 100% of the conservative treatment and diagnostic criteria under **CC-SPINE-2024**.
3. **Statutory & Clinical Standards Path:** Under **CIC § 10169.5** and **CHSC § 1374.32(b)**, the plan’s narrow focus on "hardware fracture" is legally overridden by the documented pseudarthrosis and objective C6 motor deficit, which meets the **AANS/CNS 2023 Tier 1** surgical guidelines.

**DECISION:** The denial of coverage for CPT 22551 (Revision ACDF C5-C6) is **OVERTURNED**. HealthFirst is directed to immediately approve and authorize the requested surgical procedure.

---

**Disposition:** OVERTURNED

**Warrant:**

The initial prior authorization request for an ACDF C6-C7 (CPT 22551) for member Dorothy James was denied on 2024-11-02 by Dr. Alan Foster, MD (MED-003) due to "Physical therapy requirement not met. Plan received PT records from Valley Physical Therapy documenting 4 weeks of treatment. Member claims 8 total weeks but second provider (Mountain PT) records not received by plan. Cannot verify claimed treatment without complete records."

Upon review of the submitted appeal, including the previously unreceived records from Mountain Physical Therapy, the following determination is made:

1.  **Resolution of Initial Denial Reason (Plan Criteria):** The primary reason for the initial denial was administrative, citing incomplete records regarding physical therapy. The appeal directly addresses this by submitting the records from Mountain Physical Therapy, which document an additional 4 weeks of treatment. Therefore, the member has completed a total of 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy across two providers (Valley Physical Therapy: 4 weeks; Mountain Physical Therapy: 4 weeks). This duration (8 weeks) exceeds HealthFirst's Clinical Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024) Section 2.2(a) which requires a "minimum 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy." Thus, the plan's stated duration requirement is now met.

2.  **Compliance with State Law – CIC § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy Requirement):**
    *   **Functional Plateau:** The clinical record clearly documents that the member reached a functional plateau during physical therapy. Valley Physical Therapy noted "Moderate improvement then plateau," and Mountain Physical Therapy documented "No improvement in neurological symptoms. Plateau documented by PT at discharge." California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(2) explicitly states that a health insurer shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy where "The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms." This provision overrides any plan requirement for further physical therapy.
    *   **Structural Neurological Compromise:** The clinical record demonstrates objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address. The MRI reveals a "C6-C7 large disc herniation, bilateral C7 nerve root compression, bilateral foraminal stenosis, mild cord contact without compression." The neurological exam confirms "Bilateral C7 dermatomal symptoms: bilateral tricep weakness 4/5, bilateral tricep reflex diminished, bilateral finger tingling." Physical therapy at Mountain PT specifically noted "No improvement in neurological symptoms." CIC § 10169.5(a)(3) dictates that a plan cannot require PT completion when "The condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address." This condition is met.

3.  **Adherence to Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS, NASS, AO Spine):**
    *   **Myelopathy/Myeloradiculopathy Features:** While the treating diagnosis is "Cervical radiculopathy C6-C7, bilateral," the presence of bilateral C7 dermatomal symptoms, bilateral triceps weakness (4/5), diminished bilateral tricep reflexes, and "mild cord contact" on MRI points towards a more complex condition often termed myeloradiculopathy, or myelopathy with associated radiculopathy. The AANS/CNS and AO Spine guidelines emphasize that myelopathy and radiculopathy require different treatment algorithms and that applying radiculopathy-derived conservative treatment requirements to myelopathy patients is a "category error."
    *   **Efficacy of PT for Neurological Symptoms:** Clinical guidelines, including the AO Spine Guidelines (2021) and Cochrane Review (2021), state that physical therapy has limited efficacy for moderate-severe myelopathy and specifically does "NOT produce meaningful functional improvement" for neurological symptoms. They also highlight that "There is no high-quality evidence supporting a mandatory course of physical therapy prior to surgical intervention for patients with moderate to severe cervical myelopathy. Delaying surgery in such patients... may result in neurological deterioration." The member's documented lack of improvement in neurological symptoms during PT is consistent with this understanding.
    *   **Surgical Indication:** Per AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023), surgical indications are met under Tier 1(b) ("Progressive neurological deficit despite conservative treatment" – patient's bilateral weakness and diminished reflexes persist despite 8 weeks PT) and Tier 2(b) & (c) ("Radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks conservative tx" and "Significant functional impairment not responding to conservative care").

**Conclusion:**

The initial denial was based on a documentation deficiency that has been rectified. With the complete records, the member has not only met HealthFirst's 6-week minimum physical therapy requirement (having completed 8 weeks) but has also demonstrated a clear functional plateau, particularly regarding neurological symptoms. Crucially, California State Law (CIC § 10169.5) explicitly prohibits plans from denying surgery based on unmet PT requirements when a functional plateau has been reached or when structural neurological compromise exists that PT cannot address. Furthermore, generally accepted clinical standards support surgical intervention for patients with persistent, functionally impairing bilateral neurological deficits that have not responded to an adequate course of conservative treatment.

Applying the hierarchy of authority (State Law > Clinical Standard > Plan Criteria), both state law and clinical standards dictate that the requested ACDF is medically necessary and should be approved.

**The prior authorization denial is hereby OVERTURNED.**

The requested procedure (ACDF C6-C7, CPT 22551) is approved for Dorothy James.

HealthFirst PPO Gold

# PRIOR AUTHORIZATION APPEAL DETERMINATION

**Date of Determination:** November 14, 2024  
**Case ID:** PA-2024-F001  
**Member Name:** Dorothy James  
**Age:** 51  
**Health Plan:** HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441  
**State of Residence:** California  
**Coverage Effective Date:** April 1, 2019  

**Requested Procedure:** Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7, One Level (CPT 22551)  
**Requesting Provider:** Dr. Paul Adams, MD — Spine Surgery  
**Proposed Facility:** UCLA Medical Center  

**Initial Denial Date:** November 2, 2024  
**Initial Reviewer:** Dr. Alan Foster, MD  
**Denial Reason Code:** MED-003 (Physical Therapy Requirement Not Met)  

---

## I. FINAL DISPOSITION

**DECISION:** **OVERTURN THE DENIAL IN FULL**  

The Health Plan’s initial decision to deny coverage for CPT 22551 (ACDF C6-C7, one level) is **reversed**. The requested surgical procedure is medically necessary under California law, generally accepted clinical standards, and the Health Plan's own clinical coverage criteria. The plan is directed to issue an immediate authorization for the requested procedure.

---

## II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The initial denial of the requested CCDF/ACDF at C6-C7 was based on the non-receipt of physical therapy records from the member's second provider (Mountain Physical Therapy). The Health Plan asserted it could only verify 4 weeks of the contractually required 6 weeks of physical therapy. 

On appeal, the complete clinical records from Mountain Physical Therapy were submitted, confirming an additional 4 weeks (12 sessions) of physical therapy, bringing the member’s documented conservative treatment to a **total of 8 weeks (24 sessions)** across two providers. Because the missing records have been supplied, and because the member has met and exceeded all of the plan's conservative therapy and diagnostic thresholds, the initial denial is no longer supported and is overturned.

---

## III. STEP-BY-STEP EVALUATION & CLINICAL ANALYSIS

### Step 1: Procedural Adequacy and Defect Check
The initial denial notice dated November 2, 2024, issued by Dr. Alan Foster, MD, was evaluated against the statutory requirements of **California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b)**. 
*   **Finding:** The denial notice was procedurally adequate. It specified the precise clinical reason for the denial (non-receipt of Mountain PT records resulting in failure to verify the 6-week conservative trial) and referenced the clinical criteria applied (MED-003). Therefore, the review proceeds to a substantive clinical and statutory evaluation.

### Step 2: Clinical Classification and Diagnostic Verification (Myelopathy vs. Radiculopathy)
To apply the correct clinical standard, the member's pathology must be accurately classified.
*   **Imaging Findings (MRI, September 1, 2024):** Demonstrates a large disc herniation at C6-C7, bilateral C7 nerve root compression, and bilateral foraminal stenosis. Crucially, the MRI notes *"mild cord contact without compression"* and no cord signal changes (myelomalacia).
*   **Neurological Examination (September 5, 2024):** Documents bilateral C7 dermatomal symptoms including bilateral triceps weakness (4/5), diminished bilateral triceps reflexes, and bilateral finger tingling. No upper motor neuron signs (such as hyperreflexia, Hoffman's sign, clonus, or gait instability) are documented.
*   **Diagnostic Classification:** Because there is no objective evidence of spinal cord compression, myelomalacia, or upper motor neuron signs, this case is classified as **Bilateral Cervical Radiculopathy at C6-C7**. It does not meet the clinical definition of cervical myelopathy. Therefore, the specialized Myelopathy Exceptions (such as HealthFirst Exception 2.2(a) or DMHC APL 22-014) do not apply. The case must be evaluated under the standard clinical pathways for cervical radiculopathy.

### Step 3: Plan Criteria and Exception Application (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024)
Applying the standard criteria under **HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2**, the clinical record demonstrates complete compliance as follows:

1.  **Section 2.1 (Diagnosis Requirement):** The member has a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy with corresponding bilateral C7 dermatomal weakness, reflex changes, and sensory symptoms. Supported by an MRI within 6 months (September 1, 2024) showing structural pathology (C6-C7 herniation and nerve root compression) matching clinical findings. **(MET)**
2.  **Section 2.2(a) (Physical Therapy):** The plan requires a minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy. 
    *   *Valley Physical Therapy:* June 1, 2024, to June 28, 2024 (4 weeks, 12 sessions) — Documented moderate improvement followed by a plateau. *(Received initially)*
    *   *Mountain Physical Therapy:* July 15, 2024, to August 9, 2024 (4 weeks, 12 sessions) — Documented no improvement in neurological symptoms with a discharge plateau. *(Submitted with Appeal)*
    *   *Total Combined:* **8 weeks (24 sessions)** of supervised physical therapy are now fully documented and verified. This exceeds the 6-week plan requirement. **(MET)**
3.  **Section 2.2(b) (Pharmacotherapy):** The plan requires a trial of at least two designated agents for a minimum of 4 weeks each.
    *   *Agent 1:* Pregabalin 150mg BID (neuropathic agent) for 3 months (partial relief).
    *   *Agent 2:* Naproxen 500mg BID (NSAID) for 2 months (inadequate response).
    *   Both trials exceeded 4 weeks. **(MET)**
4.  **Section 2.2(c) (Interventional Treatment):** The member underwent a bilateral C7 epidural steroid injection on September 20, 2024, resulting in only temporary relief (50% left-sided, 30% right-sided) before returning to baseline. **(MET)**

**Conclusion under Plan Criteria:** With the submission of the Mountain PT records on appeal, the member has satisfied 100% of the medical necessity criteria outlined in HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024.

### Step 4: Statutory and Regulatory Alignment (California Law Override)
Under the **Hierarchy of Authority**, California state law supersedes any restrictive plan interpretations.
*   **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(2):** This statute prohibits a health plan from mechanically conditioning approval of a surgical procedure on physical therapy compliance when the member has completed physical therapy and the treating clinician documents that the member reached a **functional plateau** without adequate symptom resolution.
*   **Application:** Both the Valley PT and Mountain PT records explicitly document a clinical plateau. Specifically, the Mountain PT discharge summary notes *"no improvement in neurological symptoms"* and confirms a discharge plateau. Denying authorization when a functional plateau has been reached across 8 weeks of therapy is a direct violation of CIC § 10169.5.

### Step 5: Clinical Standards Review (AANS/CNS, NASS, AO Spine)
Under **CHSC § 1374.32(b)** (the Independent Medical Review standard), a service must be approved if it is in accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice, regardless of more restrictive internal plan criteria.
*   According to the **American Association of Neurological Surgeons / Congress of Neurological Surgeons (AANS/CNS) 2023 Guidelines** and the **North American Spine Society (NASS) 2020 Guidelines**, single-level ACDF (CPT 22551) is a strongly supported, Tier 2 indicated procedure for patients with cervical radiculopathy who exhibit objective neurological deficits (such as 4/5 motor weakness and diminished reflexes) and have failed a conservative trial of 6–12 weeks consisting of physical therapy, pharmacotherapy, and interventional pain management.
*   Dorothy James exhibits objective bilateral motor weakness (4/5 triceps strength) and reflex loss corresponding directly to C6-C7 compression. She has undergone an exhaustive 8-week course of physical therapy, 3 months of neuropathic medication, and a cervical epidural steroid injection without long-term benefit. Requiring any further delay or conservative measures is contrary to clinical evidence and exposes the member to risks of permanent neurological deficit.

---

## IV. CONCLUSION AND ORDER

The clinical information submitted on appeal resolves the administrative omission that led to the initial denial. The patient has completed 8 weeks of physical therapy, which has been verified through primary records. Because the patient has bilateral, symptomatic, MRI-confirmed C6-C7 radiculopathy with objective motor deficits that have failed exhaustive conservative therapy, the requested procedure is medically necessary under plan guidelines, California law, and national clinical standards.

The Health Plan is hereby **ORDERED** to:
1.  **Overturn** the denial of prior authorization for CPT 22551 (ACDF C6-C7, one level).
2.  **Approve and authorize** the requested procedure to be performed by Dr. Paul Adams at UCLA Medical Center.
3.  Issue the formal authorization number and notice to the member and provider within the legally mandated timeframes under **CHSC § 1367.01**.

***

**Reviewer Signature:**  
*Expert Medical Appeals Reviewer*  
*Board Certified in Neurological Surgery*  
*State of California Department of Managed Health Care / Independent Medical Review Panelist*

FINAL DISPOSITION: PARTIAL

HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN
APPEAL DETERMINATION DIVISION
PO Box 45000, San Francisco, CA 94145

Date: November 20, 2024

Member Name: Victor Patel
Member ID: M-667799
Plan: HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
State of Residence: California
Case ID: PA-2024-E001
Appeal Date: November 18, 2024

Requesting Provider: Dr. Lisa Park, MD — Spine Surgery, UCSF Medical Center
Requested Procedure: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF), C5-C6 and C6-C7 (CPT 22551 and CPT 22552)
Original Denial Date: November 1, 2024
Original Reviewer: Dr. Patricia Huang, MD

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FINAL APPEAL DETERMINATION: PARTIAL OVERTURN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dear Mr. Patel and Dr. Park,

HealthFirst Health Plan has completed its clinical and regulatory review of the first-level appeal submitted on November 18, 2024, regarding the prior authorization denial for a two-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 and C6-C7. 

Based on a comprehensive review of the clinical records, the HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024), California statutory and regulatory mandates, and generally accepted clinical guidelines, we have reached the following determination:

1. C5-C6 LEVEL (CPT 22551): The prior authorization denial is OVERTURNED. Surgical intervention at the C5-C6 level is APPROVED.
2. C6-C7 LEVEL (CPT 22552): The prior authorization denial is UPHELD. Surgical intervention at the C6-C7 level is DENIED.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLINICAL AND REGULATORY RATIONALE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I. ANALYSIS OF C5-C6 LEVEL (CPT 22551) — OVERTURNED (APPROVED)

The clinical documentation submitted demonstrates that the member meets all plan criteria, regulatory requirements, and clinical standards for surgical decompression and fusion at the C5-C6 level.

1. Clinical Presentation and Diagnosis:
   - The clinical record documents a primary presentation of severe right C6 radiculopathy. 
   - The neurological exam dated September 20, 2024, reveals objective neurological deficits in the C6 distribution: right bicep weakness graded at 3+/5, an absent right bicep reflex, and right C6 dermatomal numbness and tingling.
   - This satisfies HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.1(a) (Cervical radiculopathy with nerve root compression and radicular symptoms) and Section 2.1(c) (Cervical disc herniation with objective neurological deficit).

2. Imaging Findings:
   - The cervical spine MRI dated September 15, 2024, demonstrates a large disc herniation at C5-C6 causing moderate-to-severe right C6 nerve root compression and foraminal stenosis.
   - This satisfies CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.3 (Imaging Requirement), which requires current imaging demonstrating structural pathology consistent with the member's symptoms and proposed surgical level.

3. Conservative Treatment:
   - The member completed 8 weeks (24 sessions) of supervised physical therapy directed at the cervical spine, with persistent C6 symptoms.
   - Pharmacotherapy trials included Pregabalin 150mg BID for 4 months (neuropathic agent) and Naproxen 500mg BID for 3 months (NSAID), satisfying the requirement for two agents tried for at least 4 weeks.
   - The member underwent a right C6 epidural steroid injection on October 15, 2024, which provided 70% temporary relief but symptoms fully returned within 4 weeks.
   - This satisfies CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2 (Conservative Treatment Requirement), including physical therapy, pharmacotherapy, and interventional treatment.
   - Furthermore, under California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(3), a health plan cannot condition surgical approval on the completion of physical therapy when there is objective evidence of structural neurological compromise (such as the 3+/5 bicep weakness and absent reflex documented here) that physical therapy cannot address.

4. Clinical Standards:
   - Under the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) and NASS Guidelines (2020), surgical decompression is a Tier 2 (Strongly Indicated) intervention for patients with cervical radiculopathy, correlating MRI pathology, and objective neurological deficits who have failed conservative management.

Therefore, the denial of CPT 22551 for the C5-C6 level is medically unjustified and is hereby overturned.

II. ANALYSIS OF C6-C7 LEVEL (CPT 22552) — UPHELD (DENIED)

The clinical documentation submitted does not support the medical necessity of extending the fusion to the C6-C7 level at this time.

1. Clinical Presentation and Diagnosis:
   - The neurological exam dated September 20, 2024, notes only a "slightly diminished" right tricep reflex, with "no definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms." 
   - The physical therapy discharge summary at week 8 explicitly notes that C7 symptoms were "minimal and possibly resolving."
   - This fails to establish a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy at the C7 level under CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.1.

2. Imaging Findings:
   - The MRI dated September 15, 2024, shows only a "small disc bulge" and "mild foraminal narrowing" at C6-C7, with "no nerve root compression identifiable" and "no cord contact."
   - This fails CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.3 and Section 3.3 (Exclusions), which mandate that imaging must demonstrate pathology at the proposed surgical level consistent with the clinical presentation.

3. Conservative Treatment:
   - While conservative therapy was completed for the cervical spine generally, no C7-specific interventional treatment (such as a C7-specific epidural or selective nerve root block) was performed to confirm the C6-C7 level as a symptomatic pain generator.

4. Clinical Standards:
   - Under the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) and NASS Guidelines (2020), surgical intervention at a level with mild imaging findings, resolving or absent dermatomal symptoms, and no objective nerve root compression is classified as Tier 3 (Surgery Not Indicated).
   - Prophylactic fusion of an adjacent level to "prevent accelerated degeneration" in the absence of correlating clinical and radiographic pathology is not supported by clinical evidence.

Therefore, the denial of CPT 22552 for the C6-C7 level is upheld.

III. RESOLUTION OF PROCEDURAL DEFECT IN INITIAL DENIAL

Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31, a health plan must provide specific clinical criteria and reasons for any denial. The initial denial notice dated November 1, 2024, issued by Dr. Patricia Huang, MD, denied the entire two-level request because "Two-level fusion [is] not approved when one level meets criteria and one does not."

Denying an entire surgical request—including a level (C5-C6) that clearly and unambiguously meets all medical necessity criteria—solely because an adjacent requested level (C6-C7) does not meet criteria is a procedural defect. Under CHSC § 1374.32, health plans must evaluate medical necessity for each requested service. Denying the medically necessary C5-C6 decompression and fusion based on the non-conformance of C6-C7 violates California's medical necessity standard. This appeal determination corrects that defect by issuing a partial approval.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SUMMARY OF DISPOSITION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- CPT Code 22551 (ACDF, Single Level, C5-C6): APPROVED
- CPT Code 22552 (ACDF, Additional Level, C6-C7): DENIED

Dr. Park may proceed with scheduling the single-level C5-C6 ACDF (CPT 22551). This authorization is valid for 90 days from the date of this letter (expiring February 18, 2025) per CC-SPINE-2024, Section 3.5.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOTICE OF INDEPENDENT MEDICAL REVIEW (IMR) RIGHTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If you disagree with the denied portion of this decision (the denial of CPT 22552 for the C6-C7 level), you have the right to request an Independent Medical Review (IMR) from the California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) under California Health & Safety Code § 1374.30.

- There is no fee to apply for an IMR.
- You may submit an application for IMR if the plan's decision has been upheld on appeal.
- For standard cases, the IMR organization will reach a decision within 30 days of receiving your application and supporting documentation.
- To apply, you may complete the IMR Application Form available on the DMHC website (www.dmhc.ca.gov) or call the DMHC Help Center at 1-888-466-2219.

Sincerely,

Clinical Appeals Committee
HealthFirst Health Plan
California Licensed Medical Director
